tools.name: read_content
tools.description:
Read a module's, template's or layout's body with line numbers — the Read step before a surgical `edit_content` (NOT `update_modules_many`). PREFER over `list_modules` (metadata only).
- `entityKind:"layout"` = chrome shell its templates render in (`list_templates` shows each template's layoutId).
- Omit `field` -> every body; name one to window a large body via `offset` (1-based line) + `limit`.
- Each block prints `sha=`; pass it to `edit_content` as `expectedSha` to guard against concurrent changes.

tools.name: edit_content
tools.description:
Surgical string-replace in a module's, template's or layout's `html`/`css`/`js` — cheap, minimal-diff edits of existing code.
PREFER over `update_modules_many` for targeted changes; use `update_modules_many` for wholesale rewrites, new modules, or `fields`/`displayName`/`kind` changes.
CORE RULES:
- Read the body first with `read_content`. Edits apply in order, all-or-nothing.
- Success returns the NEW `sha=` + line-numbered snippets of changed regions: chain further `edit_content` calls with that sha and the fresh line numbers, WITHOUT re-reading.
- Templates/layouts are APPROVAL-GATED: you propose, the Owner clicks Approve on the card. Do not claim such an edit was applied.
- INTERNAL LINKS (`html` hrefs, `url`/`link` fields, list-entry links): write the page path (e.g. `/about`). Target MUST be an existing page (`list_pages`) or it is refused — create an empty shell first (`build_page({page:{slug, title}, modules:[]})`) or link after. `/` and `/#section` are always valid. Exception: links to pages of this chat's site-import run are kept and resolved by `resolve_import_links` at the end. Media/files: media URL (`find_media`). External: full `https://` URL.

oldString.description: Exact text from `read_content` (incl. whitespace); must be UNIQUE in the body (add context) unless `replaceAll:true`. `""` fills an EMPTY field (e.g. no js yet); refused on a non-empty field.

expectedSha.description: `sha=` from `read_content` or the last edit; guards against a concurrent change.

tools.name: grep_content
tools.description: Search all module, template and layout bodies for a string or regex — find WHERE to edit before `read_content` + `edit_content` ('change X everywhere', locate a class/string). Result lines: `<kind> <slug> (<id>) <field>:<lineNo>: <text>`.

pattern.description: Literal substring, or JS regex with `isRegex:true`.

tools.name: patch_page_module_fields
tools.description:
Change individual values of ONE placement (a heading, one local-`list` entry's text or link, a `url`/`image` field); all other values stay untouched.
USE FOR: targeted wording fixes ('fix Welcom in the hero', 'rename the 2nd menu item to Pricing', a chip naming `placement=(blockName, position), field=…[entry]`).
DO NOT USE FOR: replacing placements' values wholesale or setting nested modules -> `set_page_module_content_many`; structure -> `update_modules_many`.
CORE RULES:
- Several edits of one placement go in one call (all or none).
- SYNCED placement (content shared with other pages) needs `scope`: `everywhere` = every page showing it | `here` = detach this page first, change only it. Ask the operator when unclear.
E.g. `{pageId, blockName:"content", position:0, edits:[{field:"hero_title", text:"Welcome"}, {field:"nav_items", item:"<entry id>", key:"label", text:"Pricing"}]}`

item.description: Entry id in a local `list` field.

text.description: New value: plain text for text fields (HTML-escaped for you — never markup); path / https URL for `url`/`image` fields and link targets.

tools.name: build_page
tools.description:
Build a WHOLE page in ONE transaction: create (`page:{slug, title}`) or target existing (`page:{pageId}`) + the full ordered module list (each entry places one module into a template block, top to bottom; on an existing page entries append). Any invalid entry aborts everything (error names `modules[i]` + failing field); nothing is written. USE FOR: every page creation (THE page-creation tool); any page needing >1 module — never `add_module` / `create_content_instances` chains. `modules: []` = intentionally empty page shell. DO NOT USE FOR: one incremental module on an existing page -> `add_module` (target `page`); site chrome header/footer -> `add_module` (target `layout`; chrome never rides in a page body). CORE RULES: - Creating: set `page.pageType` (+ `properties`/`terms`), `page.metaDescription`, and `status:"published"` for a page that belongs on the site — a Stage refuses published pages without a description and builds only published ones; the result says what still blocks a Stage. - Per module, two modes: `moduleId` places an EXISTING module (`list_modules`; reuse first — shared modules keep pages consistent), or mint with `displayName` + `html` + `description` + `kind` + explicit `fields[]` (all required). - Pair `{{field_name}}` placeholders in `html` with `fields[]` in semantic snake_case (`hero_title`, `primary_cta_href`); never heuristic names (`cta2label2`) or numbered scalars (`label1`..`label10` -> ONE `list` field or a `module-list`). - Nested modules in the SAME call: inner entry gets `ref` and NO `blockName` (detached: minted + content-bound, not placed); the outer module's `module`/`module-list` field value references it as `{"$ref":""}`, any array order. Never an `add_module` -> `remove_module_from` -> `create_content_instances` chain. E.g. `modules:[{ref:'btn', displayName:'Button', html:'', fields:[…], content:{source:'inline', values:{label:'Go'}}}, {blockName:'content', displayName:'CTA', html:'
{{>cta}}
', fields:[{name:'cta', kind:'module', label:'CTA', allowedModuleTypes:['button']}], content:{source:'inline', values:{cta:{'$ref':'btn'}}}}]` - Zero templates on the site -> bootstrap first (`create_layout` -> `create_template`). - INTERNAL LINKS (`html` hrefs, `url`/`link` fields, list-entry links): write the page path (e.g. `/about`). Target MUST be an existing page (`list_pages`) or it is refused — create an empty shell first (`build_page({page:{slug, title}, modules:[]})`) or link after. `/` and `/#section` are always valid. Exception: links to pages of this chat's site-import run are kept and resolved by `resolve_import_links` at the end. Media/files: media URL (`find_media`). External: full `https://` URL. Typical call: `{page:{slug:'pricing', title:'Pricing', status:'published', metaDescription:'…'}, modules:[{blockName:'content', displayName:'Pricing Hero', kind:'hero', description:'…', html:'

{{hero_title}}

', fields:[{name:'hero_title', kind:'text', label:'Hero title'}], content:{source:'inline', values:{hero_title:'Fair pricing'}}}, …]}`

page.description: Existing: `{pageId, metaDescription?}` (modules append). New: `{slug, title, metaDescription, …}`. Never both.

slug.description: Lowercase letters, digits, hyphens — no path or slash. HOMEPAGE (`/`) = `home`.

templateId.description: Omit -> the page type's default template (without `pageType`: site default).

pageType.description: What the page IS (`list_page_types`), e.g. `news` for an article, `page` for a plain page. Set it whenever the site has >1 type — page queries ('latest news') find pages by it. Omitted: the type listing `templateId`, else the site default.

properties.description: Page type property values (`list_page_types`, `*` = required), e.g. `{author:'Ada Lovelace', event_date:'2026-11-03'}`.

terms.description: Categories/tags from the page type's vocabularies (`get_list` on the vocabulary shows entry ids).

status.description: Only `published` pages build on staging. Omitted: published on a site with no published page yet, else draft.

metaDescription.description: 150–160 chars, written from the page's content (migration: the source page's). Fill-once like `autofill_page_seo_many`: with `pageId` written only when the page has none; an existing one is kept (result says so).

parentPageId.description: Create UNDER this page (`list_pages`): URL = parent URL + `/` + slug (e.g. `/seo-monitoring/alerts`). Omit for top level. Move existing pages via `move_pages`.

importPageId.description: Site migration: the source `import_pages` id. Links the page to the crawl (fidelity/inventory/media checks resolve regardless of slug) and makes the build idempotent (same id rebuilds the SAME page, never a duplicate).

blockName.description: Page-TEMPLATE block — a slot, NOT a module `kind` (usually `content`; valid set: `# Current page` for the open page, `list_templates` `pageBlocks` otherwise; a mismatch error names it). Never `header`/`footer`. OMIT for a detached nested-only entry (requires `ref`).

position.description: Default bottom: entries append in array order (a new page needs none). `top` or 0-based index inserts. Not for detached entries.

ref.description: Local handle: `{"$ref":"<ref>"}` in another entry's `module`/`module-list` field value or `moduleId` resolves to this entry's `{moduleId, contentInstanceId}`. Referenced entries are created first.

moduleId.description: EXISTING module (`list_modules`), or `{"$ref":"<handle>"}` to RE-PLACE a module minted by another entry of this call (e.g. one card module, three placements; each entry gets its own content).

html.description: Module HTML. Plain source (no CDATA or extra escaping). Placeholders: `{{field}}` primitives, `{{>field}}` single nested `module`, `{{#field}}…{{/field}}` `list` and `module-list`. Accordion, tabs, carousel, mobile-nav -> `data-caelo-ui` markup (see `js`) instead of custom JS.

css.description: Module CSS. Plain source (no CDATA or extra escaping). MUST scope every selector under the module's root class — bare selectors (`body`, `h1`, `.card`) bleed into other modules and are flagged.

js.description: Vanilla JS. Plain source (no CDATA or extra escaping). Emitted ONCE per page into a shared `

default.description: ORIGINAL value(s) replaced (never a placeholder): scalar -> value; local `list` -> entries; shared `list` -> `"caelo:list/<id>"`. Omit for `module`, `module-list`, `bind:"source"`.

items.description: texts: `{node:"text", values:{text}}` | links: `{node:"link", values:{label, link:{href}}}` | menu: `{node:"entry", values:{label, link:{href}}, children}` | custom type: its fields (`list_list_types`). Keep `id` on resend.

node.description: NODE kind, not the listType slug: "text" (texts), "link" (links), "entry" (menu).

bind.description: For `kind:"list"`: `local` (default; entries live with the placement) | `shared` (site-wide menus/nav/footer/categories/tags — check `list_lists` first, edit entries via `patch_list_items_many`, share a local list via `promote_local_list`) | `source` (generated per page; placement content may set the knobs the source marks `editable`).

source.description: Required when `bind:"source"`: `{kind:"query", editable:[knobs], defaults:{page_type, terms, parent, order, limit}}` | `{kind:"system", name:"breadcrumbs"|"children"|"siblings"|"page_terms"|"term_pages"}` (only these) | `{kind:"plugin", name}` (e.g. `consent_categories`; iterating a plugin list needs no field).

allowedModuleTypes.description: For `module`/`module-list`: whitelist of stable module `type`s (e.g. `["button"]`), NOT slugs. Widen if a valid module is rejected.

bindThemeLiterals.description: Rewrite CSS literals matching a theme token into `var(--…)`. Default true — omit unless keeping a deliberate off-palette literal.

content.description: Omit for an empty private instance to fill later. `inline` -> page-local values (routine); `shared` -> mint a REUSABLE instance other pages can bind (synced by default); `existing` -> bind an instance from `list_content_instances`. `values` keyed by field name: local `list` -> entries (`[{node:'text', values:{text:'Fast'}}]`); shared `list` -> `caelo:list/<id>`; source field -> its editable knobs; nested `module`/`module-list` -> `{"$ref":"<ref>"}` | `{moduleId, contentInstanceId}`.

tools.name: set_page_module_content_many
tools.description:
Set content values of 1..N placements (may span pages) in one transaction. Content lives in a content_instance bound to the placement.
USE FOR: page-local copy ('change the hero heading on /home to X'), a whole page's text, the same fix across pages.
DO NOT USE FOR: pages/modules not existing yet -> one `build_page` call (never `add_module` + this tool); one entry's text -> `patch_page_module_fields`; every page using the module (structure/styling/fields) -> `update_modules_many`.
CORE RULES:
- UNSYNCED placements (default) stay local. A SYNCED placement aborts the batch -> `fork_placement_content` it or deliberately `set_content_instance_values_many` (propagates everywhere), then resend.
- All-or-nothing: an invalid item aborts the batch (error names `items[i]`, the placement, the failing field); nothing is written.
- INTERNAL LINKS (`html` hrefs, `url`/`link` fields, list-entry links): write the page path (e.g. `/about`). Target MUST be an existing page (`list_pages`) or it is refused — create an empty shell first (`build_page({page:{slug, title}, modules:[]})`) or link after. `/` and `/#section` are always valid. Exception: links to pages of this chat's site-import run are kept and resolved by `resolve_import_links` at the end. Media/files: media URL (`find_media`). External: full `https://` URL.

contentValues.description: Keyed by the module's field names; fully replaces the placement's values. Missing fields -> the field's `default`; `{}` resets all. Local `list` -> entries (`[{node:"text", values:{text:"Fast"}}]`, existing entries keep `id`); shared `list` -> `caelo:list/<id>` switches the list shown (entries change via `patch_list_items_many`, on every page); source field -> editable knobs (`{limit:5}`); nested `module`/`module-list` -> `{moduleId, contentInstanceId}` | array; the module's stable `type` must be in the field's `allowedModuleTypes` when set (`list_modules` shows both).

tools.name: create_content_instances
tools.description:
Mint 1..N shared, reusable content_instances in one transaction — for content shown identically on several pages (site footer copyright, brand banner on product pages, repeated blog CTA). Bind each via `set_placement_content({syncMode:'synced'})`; edits then propagate everywhere bound.
DO NOT USE FOR: one-off per-page content -> `set_page_module_content_many` (auto-mints a private instance); creating the page/modules too -> `build_page` (its `content` mints + binds in the same call).
CORE RULES:
- BEFORE CALLING: check `list_content_instances` — a row with matching purpose + module + placement pattern -> BIND it via `set_placement_content`; duplicate shared rows defeat the point.
- All-or-nothing: an invalid item aborts the batch (error names `items[i]` + failing field); nothing is written.
- INTERNAL LINKS (`html` hrefs, `url`/`link` fields, list-entry links): write the page path (e.g. `/about`). Target MUST be an existing page (`list_pages`) or it is refused — create an empty shell first (`build_page({page:{slug, title}, modules:[]})`) or link after. `/` and `/#section` are always valid. Exception: links to pages of this chat's site-import run are kept and resolved by `resolve_import_links` at the end. Media/files: media URL (`find_media`). External: full `https://` URL.

purpose.description: Why this row is shared, one line (e.g. "Pricing CTA at the bottom of every pricing-adjacent page"); `list_content_instances` shows it for reuse-vs-fork decisions. Always set it.

values.description: Keyed by the module's field names.

tools.name: list_content_instances
tools.description:
List content_instances — values filling module placeholders (TOON rows: id, module, kind, slug, displayName, purpose, placements, parents), most-placed first; counts as this chat's draft sees them.
- `purpose` = why a shared row exists: read it BEFORE minting (`create_content_instances`); reuse a row whose purpose + module fit.
- `placements` = blast radius: >1 = SHARED, edits propagate to every bound page -> check BEFORE `set_content_instance_values_many`.
- `parents` = instances showing this one in a `module`/`module-list` field. ORPHAN (safe to delete) = placements 0 AND parents 0.
Narrow by `moduleId` / `slug` / `pageId` (instances used on that page).

tools.name: get_content_instance
tools.description: Fetch one content_instance, as this chat's draft sees it: values, placements (page path, block, position, sync_mode) and parent instances showing it in a `module`/`module-list` field. Check blast radius before `set_content_instance_values_many` and before deleting (orphan = no placements AND no parents).

tools.name: set_content_instance_values_many
tools.description:
Edit values of 1..N shared content_instances in one transaction. Each item propagates to EVERY placement bound to that instance with sync_mode `synced` (blast radius = its placement count).
USE FOR: deliberate shared-content changes — check `purpose`, sample pages, placement count first (`list_content_instances` / `get_content_instance`).
DO NOT USE FOR: an edit meant for ONE page -> `set_page_module_content_many` (unsynced placement) or `fork_placement_content` first (synced); module structure -> `update_modules_many`.
CORE RULES:
- All-or-nothing: an invalid item aborts the batch (error names `items[i]`); nothing is written.
- Optional metadata in the same write: `slug`, `displayName` (`null` clears), `purpose`.
- The result names per item where the edit now shows — relay it when the reach is wider than the operator asked for.
- INTERNAL LINKS (`html` hrefs, `url`/`link` fields, list-entry links): write the page path (e.g. `/about`). Target MUST be an existing page (`list_pages`) or it is refused — create an empty shell first (`build_page({page:{slug, title}, modules:[]})`) or link after. `/` and `/#section` are always valid. Exception: links to pages of this chat's site-import run are kept and resolved by `resolve_import_links` at the end. Media/files: media URL (`find_media`). External: full `https://` URL.

values.description: Keyed by the module's field names; fully REPLACES existing values (no merge) — read via `get_content_instance` to keep other fields. Local `list` -> entries (`[{node:"text", values:{text:"Fast"}}]`, existing entries keep `id`); shared `list` -> `caelo:list/<id>` (switches the list shown; entries via `patch_list_items_many`); source field -> editable knobs (`{limit:5}`, `{terms:[…]}` for term_pages); nested `module`/`module-list` -> `{moduleId, contentInstanceId}` | array; the module's stable `type` MUST be in the field's `allowedModuleTypes` when set (`list_modules` shows both) — reuse an allowed-type module, else create one with an allowed `type`.

purpose.description: Why this shared row exists; rewrite when the operator's intent shifts.

tools.name: delete_content_instances
tools.description:
Soft-delete 1..N ORPHAN content_instances in one transaction. Orphan = no placements AND no parent instance shows it in a `module`/`module-list` field (`list_content_instances`: placements=0, parents=0).
CORE RULES:
- ANY refused item rolls back the WHOLE batch; the refusal names the blockers:
  - placements (page path, pageId, blockName, position) -> detach each via `fork_placement_content` with those values (page keeps a private copy), then retry.
  - parents -> first remove the ref from each parent's field via `set_content_instance_values_many`.
- In a chat this lands on the draft; live changes when staged.

tools.name: set_placement_content
tools.description: Bind one placement (page + block + position) to a content_instance of the SAME module. `synced` = shares content with every placement bound to that instance (instance edits propagate); `unsynced` = page-local.

tools.name: fork_placement_content
tools.description: Detach a placement from its shared content_instance into a fresh unsynced one, to edit THIS page only without affecting other bound pages. Then apply the edit via `set_page_module_content_many` (or `set_content_instance_values_many` on the new instance).

tools.name: list_layouts
tools.description:
Layouts: UUID, slug, display name, blocks with the chrome modules placed in each (`header(main-menu)|content|footer(site-footer)`) — answers "is module X already on the layout?". Use for a layout UUID/slug (e.g. after a layout-create approval); never ask the operator to paste one.
Layout blocks = site chrome: place header/footer/nav ONCE for every page via `add_module` target='layout'. NOT `build_page` blockNames — pages place into their TEMPLATE's blocks (`list_templates` `pageBlocks`, usually `content`); the layout's `content` block is where the template renders.

tools.name: list_plugins
tools.description:
Installed plugins with `status` (Owner's decision) and `health` (what running servers make of it).
- status: `active` = Owner wants it running | `awaiting_activation` = installed + verified, nothing loaded | `disabled` = Owner stopped it.
- Availability ONLY from health: `running` = tools/skills usable now | `failing` = active but failed to load on a server (`problem` says why; NOT switched off -> tell the operator, details in `get_plugin`) | `unreported` = active, no server reported yet | `not_running` = not active. Never say a capability works while its plugin is failing.
USE FOR a capability you have no tool for (translation, forms, comments, newsletter, ratings): plugin installed-but-inactive -> TELL the operator it exists and one click at /settings/plugins turns it on. Plugins on disk that failed verification follow the table: NOT installed -> explain why + the fix.
DO NOT USE as a general capability check before routine work — your tool catalogue already reflects everything running.

tools.name: activate_plugin
tools.description:
Activate an installed-but-inactive plugin so its tools + skills become usable.
USE FOR: a request no current tool covers while `list_plugins` (or the installed-plugins note) shows a plugin providing it -> say what it enables + propose in the same turn; never send the operator to a settings screen.
DO NOT USE speculatively: activating runs code, claims URL slots, starts workers; propose only what the request needs.
After approval it loads at once, but its tools reach you NEXT turn -> end this turn saying what you will do next; don't call them yet.
APPROVAL-GATED: pauses for the operator's in-chat Approve/Reject before anything changes; do not claim it is live until approved.

Over MCP: call this tool yourself — it works here. The call queues an approval card in the operator's Caelo admin (their Live Edit chat and the pending-approvals page), waits for their Approve/Reject and returns the outcome (if the wait times out, continue with caelo_await_approval). Tell the operator you requested it and that they approve the card in Caelo; never ask them to paste a prompt into the Caelo chat to run it.

reason.description: One line why; shown on the approval card.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description:
List templates: UUID, slug, name, layout UUID, `pageBlocks`, `pageTypes` (page types allowed to use it). Use for a template id or its blocks before building a page; never ask the operator for a UUID.
`pageBlocks` = the ONLY valid `blockName` for `build_page` / `add_module` target='page' (usually `content`). Header/footer/nav are layout chrome (`list_layouts`), placed once via `add_module` target='layout'.

tools.name: list_pages
tools.description: List pages (TOON rows): path, UUID, slug, parent UUID, depth (1 = top level), title, page type (what the page IS, e.g. `news`; `list_page_types`), template UUID. URL = parent URL + '/' + slug. Inside a chat, paths show its pending moves. Use for any page UUID/path; never ask the operator to paste a UUID.

tools.name: load_skill
tools.description: Load skills' full instructions into this conversation. Call the MOMENT a task matches skills in the `## Skills` block, BEFORE the work, then follow them. They persist for the whole chat -> load each skill ONCE (never reload one already loaded). Pass EVERY skill you know you need in ONE call; a second call only for one found relevant later.

slugs.description: Exact slugs from `## Skills`. Unknown/inactive slugs are named back with the valid list.

tools.name: list_modules
tools.description:
List the module catalog (metadata, no HTML/CSS/JS): id, slug, type, kind, description, fields, placement usage.
USE FOR: a reuse candidate before placing/creating (prefer `add_module` with `moduleId` over a near-duplicate); the accepted child types before filling a `module`/`module-list` field.
Fields column: `blocks:module-list allowed=faq/cta` -> child `type` must be one of them (`allowed=any` = unrestricted). `nav:list(menu) shared=main-nav` = shared list (edit entries via `patch_list_items_many`) | `items:list(texts) local` = entries per placement | `latest:list(links) source=query(…)`.

tools.name: save_design_draft
tools.description:
Save ONE design draft; drafts live here, never paste draft HTML into chat.
USE FOR: design proposals, a redesign, 'options' for something existing -> draft variants first (design-preview skill); never restyle live modules to demo ideas.
DO NOT USE FOR: a concrete small instruction ('make the button red') -> edit directly.
CORE RULES: one round = one set: the first save returns `variantSetId`; pass it on every sibling save, then call `present_design_variants`. Revise after feedback = a NEW draft in the same set, same direction, rationale noting the change.

html.description: scope `site`: complete self-contained single-file page for one direction (all CSS inline, real copy, no external scripts/images). scope `page`/`module`: a FRAGMENT restyling the target: its section markup + one `<style>` block using the site's `var(--…)` theme tokens, with the target's REAL copy and imagery; previewed inside the real theme shell, so invented token names render visibly broken.

scope.description: Default `site` (Genesis / full redesign). `page`/`module` = variant of an existing surface.

targetPageId.description: Required for scope `page` (the page redesigned); optional context for `module`.

variantSetId.description: Omit on a round's first save (minted + returned); pass it on every sibling save.

sourceKind.description: Default `genesis`. Site scope only, when the operator supplied the design: `byod_image` = your faithful reproduction of their attached mockup (needs `referenceAssetId`; the parity gate verifies against THEIR image) | `byod_html` = HTML they provided (scripts are stripped; tell them if theirs relied on scripts).

tools.name: list_design_drafts
tools.description: List design drafts' metadata (id, scope, target, variant set, direction, rationale, status, size; never HTML). Filter to see one comparison round. Use before drafting new variants, or to get the draftId for `select_design_draft` after the operator picked.

tools.name: select_design_draft
tools.description:
Mark ONE draft as chosen in its variant set, ONLY after the operator EXPLICITLY picked (variant card, /design/genesis, or in words); the choice is never yours. Re-selecting later is one call (the previous one reverts to candidate).
After a SITE draft: derive the theme from its actual palette/typography (`propose_create_theme`), build pages re-expressing its sections, never a different design. After a PAGE/MODULE variant: materialise on the chat branch (`update_modules_many` / the page's modules), transferring the token-bound fragment faithfully (`inspect_design_draft({draftId, includeHtml:true})` returns it).

tools.name: present_design_variants
tools.description:
Render a saved variant set INLINE IN CHAT, each draft previewed in the site's real theme with a pick button. Call ONCE after saving all of a round's drafts via `save_design_draft` (prefer 2–4; one option is a confirmation, not a choice).
Then END YOUR TURN: the pick arrives as the operator's next message (with the draft id) -> `select_design_draft`, then materialise. Prose feedback instead -> save revised drafts into the SAME set, present again.

tools.name: inspect_design_draft
tools.description:
Read a design draft as a FACT BASE: distinct colors (usage counts, properties), gradients, font families, font-size/spacing/radius histograms, shadows, section outline.
Materialising: SITE draft -> derive the theme from THIS inventory (exact palette/typefaces, never invent others), then re-express the outline's sections as modules. Page/module variant -> the fragment is token-bound; transfer it faithfully.

draftId.description: Omit for the selected SITE draft; page/module variants need it.

includeHtml.description: Only when you need the markup (building/editing modules); the inventory answers every theming question far cheaper.

tools.name: inspect_external_page
tools.description:
Fetch ONE page of an EXTERNAL site (operator's existing site, a reference) returning only the requested `facets`. Keep discovery turns small, template turns rich.
USE FOR: understanding a page -> `{}` (+ `links` on the FIRST/homepage inspect); building a template from a sample -> `screenshot`, `tokens`, `altTexts`, `images` + markdown, plus `query_page_html` for specific sections.
DO NOT USE FOR: raw HTML (no such facet; bounded `query_page_html` by selector or `describe`, never dump a whole page) | page-type map (`map_external_page_types`) | whole sites, no link-following (`propose_site_import`) | Caelo's own pages (`inspect_page_render`). Public http(s) only; private/internal addresses refused (SSRF guard).

stripBoilerplate.description: Default true: cookie/consent banners, hidden DOM (mobile-nav clones, offscreen slides; rendered path) and same-page repeated blocks are stripped from markdown + meta outline, with counts reported. Top-level, not a facet. false = verbatim (when cleanup removed something you need). `query_page_html` and inventory facets (links, altTexts, images, tokens) always see the full DOM.

markdown.description: Readable text as Markdown; truncated with a cursor -> `read_page_more` for the rest.

meta.description: Title, description, canonical, lang + hreflang, h1–h3 outline.

links.description: Outbound links {href, text, rel, location nav|footer|body}. Index/nav pages carry 200+ -> only on the first/homepage inspect (site structure), off for content inspects.

altTexts.description: img alt + aria-label inventory; with `images` on, only aria-labels (no double-listing).

images.description: Top ~20 asset URLs (img, CSS backgrounds, video/audio/source) ranked by prominence, each with alt; feed to `import_media_from_urls`. Complete list of a crawled run: `list_page_assets({runId, search})`.

screenshot.description: Full-page render attached to your next turn.

tokens.description: Design token inventory (rendered computed styles when Chromium is available, else static CSS).

tools.name: read_page_more
tools.description: Continue reading the Markdown of a page fetched with `inspect_external_page` (cached: no re-fetch, no fetch-budget cost). Returns the next 8000-char slice + next cursor (or a done marker). Expired handle -> re-run `inspect_external_page`.

cursor.description: Char offset from the previous slice's truncation note; omit = 0.

tools.name: query_page_html
tools.description:
Pull ONE specific part of an external page's HTML without loading the whole page. Pass exactly ONE mode: `keyword` | `cssSelector` | `xpath` | `describe`.
USE FOR: one section -> prefer over `inspect_external_page`'s `markup` facet (whole page).

Over this connection the install's AI is not used: the AI part comes back to you — a work item to answer with your own model and send back through the tool it names, or an `AiDelegated:` answer that says what to do instead (see caelo_get_context).

url.description: Absolute public URL; only without a pageRef.

keyword.description: Exact text; returns HTML window(s) around each hit.

describe.description: Natural language, e.g. 'the pricing table', 'each product card's title + price'; a small model extracts it from the full HTML so only that enters your context.

contextChars.description: keyword mode: chars around each hit; default 800.

tools.name: screenshot_external_page
tools.description:
Render ONE page of an EXTERNAL site in headless Chromium; you see the image this turn (analyse it next step; do not end the turn to wait).
USE FOR: with `inspect_external_page` when an operator names their existing site (inventory = facts, this = visual impression for the keep-design question).
DO NOT USE FOR: Caelo's own pages (`screenshot_page`); looping over many URLs (propose the crawl: `propose_site_import`).
Public http(s) URLs only; private/internal refused. Missing Playwright/Chromium -> fails loudly: tell the operator, never pretend you saw the page.

fullPage.description: Default true (whole page incl. long pages); false = viewport-only 1280×800 glance.

tools.name: map_external_page_types
tools.description:
Turn an EXTERNAL site's homepage into its page-type map: distinct types (pricing, blog-article, use-cases, …), each with ONE representative sample URL to build a template from + WHY it was classified (name it to the operator). Sources: nav + footer links + sampled sitemap.xml.
USE FOR: migration step 1, right after glancing at the homepage (cheap alternative to crawling). Then sample each type with `inspect_external_page` and build its template.
DO NOT USE FOR: crawling the whole site (`propose_site_import`) before this.
Noise filtered: other-locale prefixes (/de when migrating /en), /tag, /category, date archives (/2023/05/…), /author, pagination. Many /blog/* collapse into ONE 'blog-article' type. Public http(s) URLs only; private addresses refused.

url.description: Exact base being migrated (e.g. `https://example.com/en`); fixes host + active locale.

includeSitemap.description: Also sample sitemap.xml for types nav/footer miss. Default true.

sitemapSampleSize.description: Sitemap URLs to sample (not enumerate). Default 40, max 200.

scopePathPrefix.description: Pass when the operator wants one language/section (e.g. `/de/`): only URLs under it are sampled; the rest is reported out-of-scope.

tools.name: get_import_page_screenshot
tools.description: Attach a crawled import page's stored screenshot of the ORIGINAL site (crawl time) to your next turn — visual reference to compare your rebuild against. A missing screenshot (crawl without screenshots) is reported -> never claim you saw it. Caelo pages -> `screenshot_page`; live URLs -> `screenshot_external_page`.

tools.name: get_import_page
tools.description:
Read ONE crawled page's GIST to rebuild it with `build_page` without re-fetching: proposed slug + title, text as Markdown (truncated with cursor -> `read_page_more`), design tokens (measured samples, else actually-used values — cite THESE, don't guess), and a `pageRef` for `query_page_html` to pull one section of the FULL stored HTML (stripped parts stay reachable). Never returns raw page-builder HTML.
DO NOT USE FOR: the visual -> `get_import_page_screenshot`; a live URL not in a crawl -> `inspect_external_page`.
Default view strips layout-owned chrome (header/footer/nav), consent noise, duplicate mobile-nav DOM, unreferenced `--wp--preset--*` tokens, reported under 'Stripped from this read'. Chrome binds ONCE at layout/template — never rebuild it per page.

importPageId.description: Staging import_pages id (`list_import_pages`), built page id, or slug-matched built page; the result echoes the resolved staging id.

fullPage.description: true = full stored capture incl. chrome + raw token dump — only when rebuilding header/footer itself.

tools.name: list_import_pages
tools.description:
List a crawl run's status + its pages with `importPageId` (the id every per-page import tool takes), source url, proposed slug/title, rebuild status, built page id — never crawled HTML (-> `get_import_page`).
USE FOR:
- Polling after the operator approves `propose_site_import`: run `crawling` -> wait, re-check; continue at `ready_for_review`.
- Before rebuilding: `importPageId` for `get_import_page`, `build_page` `page.importPageId` (links the build for verification + run report), `check_page_content_inventory`, `get_import_page_screenshot`, `add_import_page_notes`.
Never guess or reuse ids from other runs.

status.description: `pending` not yet rebuilt | `accepted` linked to a built page | `rejected` declined by the operator.

search.description: Find a page: case-insensitive substring over source url, proposed slug, title.

limit.description: Default 200. Raise for crawls >200 pages; the result names the matched total.

tools.name: add_import_page_notes
tools.description: Record findings from rebuilding an imported page for the operator's migration report: typos (fix obvious ones, applied:true), dead links, missing alt texts, thin content, improvement ideas (applied:false — operator decides). BATCH a page's notes in ONE call. Record honestly, incl. what you could not fix.

importPageId.description: EITHER the staging import_pages id OR the built CMS page id (from build_page / accept_import_pages); both resolve.

applied.description: true = fixed during rebuild; false = suggestion.

tools.name: get_import_run_report
tools.description: Migration run rollup: pages built per confirmed type, redirects, crawl fetch errors, your notes (applied vs suggested per category). Call when the migration is DONE; close by narrating it plainly (preserved, fixed, what to check) — never paste raw data.

tools.name: get_link_migration_report
tools.description:
Read-only report of the one-time link migration (old plain-path links converted to page references): links converted per place + every link it could NOT convert (matched no page/media; never guessed) with its module/content.
USE FOR: operator asks about broken/old links after an update; before fixing links site-wide. Current link problems -> `check_links`.
Fix each with `update_modules_many` / `set_content_instance_values_many`: point it at an existing page path (`list_pages`) or remove it. A link in a layout's own HTML is the Owner's (Settings -> Layouts): name the layout + path. Running/reverting the migration is the Owner's (Settings -> Internal links).

search.description: Matches the link, its label and field.

tools.name: set_migration_budget
tools.description:
Propose a migration run's money ceiling in the operator's currency. Approving an import already arms one from the estimate's high end -> call only when the operator names a DIFFERENT amount, or to RAISE it after the gate paused the run ('Cost ceiling reached'), which re-arms it so the run continues. Never propose an amount the operator has not named; the click confirms their number. Track spend with `check_run_budget`.
APPROVAL-GATED: recorded only after the operator clicks Approve on the in-chat card; never claim it applied or proceed as if the higher ceiling were in force.

Over MCP: when this call needs the operator's approval, it queues an approval card in their Caelo admin (Live Edit chat and the pending-approvals page) and returns the outcome once they decide — tell them to approve the card; never ask them to paste a prompt into the Caelo chat.

ceiling.description: Whole-run budget in major units (10 = €10), not per page.

currency.description: Letter code the operator named, e.g. EUR.

tools.name: check_run_budget
tools.description:
Check a migration run's cumulative AI spend (orchestrator + all subagents) vs the operator's confirmed budget, plus a progress-weighted estimate of the cost to finish.
PAUSE-AND-ASK gate, not auto-stop: call BEFORE each rebuild batch. Ceiling crossed -> finish the page in flight, dispatch no new batches, show the operator done / spent / extrapolated cost to finish, ask: raise the budget (`set_migration_budget`) or stop. Never keep spending past the ceiling silently; never claim done while pages remain and the budget is blown.

tools.name: check_page_content_inventory
tools.description:
Verify a rebuilt imported page lost NO source content — call right AFTER rebuilding it with `build_page`. Returns coverage + a LOUD list of every missing heading, paragraph, list item, image, link or CTA (with source context).
Content is sacred: restore anything genuinely dropped, or record WHY via `add_import_page_notes` — never let content vanish silently.

importPageId.description: Staging import_pages id (`list_import_pages` / `get_import_page`; ALWAYS resolves) OR built CMS page id (matched via build_page's importPageId link, slug, or home-page designation). Built page not found (custom/translated slug) -> pass the staging id; import data never expires, a miss = id/slug mismatch.

includeChrome.description: Include source header/footer; default false — chrome is verified once at the layout.

tools.name: detect_import_boilerplate
tools.description:
Find content blocks repeating across a crawled run's pages (CTA banners, newsletter boxes, breadcrumb zones, author bios, in-content nav). BOILERPLATE: rebuild each as ONE shared module at the suggested level (layout = site-wide chrome | template = per-page-type block | shared content_instance = fixed block on a page subset), never copied into every page. Call AFTER clustering, BEFORE rebuilding pages.
Returns per candidate: page count, fixed vs per-page text (breadcrumbs vary -> template values fill per page), suggested placement + reason.

minPages.description: Min pages a block must recur on. Default 3.

tools.name: get_page_log
tools.description: Read a page's durable work log BEFORE changing it (why edited, decisions, operator answers, open questions); essential when starting fresh, e.g. as a subagent. Newest-first, default 20 entries; empty is normal. Record your own meaningful change with `log_page_edit`.

tools.name: log_page_edit
tools.description: Append WHY you changed a page to its durable log, so later chats/subagents know the intent without this conversation. Call after a MEANINGFUL change only — one entry per real decision; no routine no-ops or per-tool-call narration. Append-only; never reviewed or reverted.

entryKind.description: edited = substantive content/module change | decision = your call + rationale | operator_answer = operator answer that shaped the page | open_question = unresolved, a later turn must settle | rebuilt = from scratch | note = other durable note.

summary.description: One plain sentence: what happened/was decided and why.

detail.description: Structured extras as an OBJECT (not scalar): chosen option, operator's exact words, affected module ids.

tools.name: site_memory_propose
tools.description: Propose an addition to the site's AI memory; queues for Owner review, effective only if accepted.

tools.name: bug_report
tools.description:
File a bug against Caelo ITSELF when a tool/surface contradicts its documented contract (result contradicts persisted state, render ignores a parameter, error on input the description calls valid).
DO NOT USE FOR: your own mistakes (wrong args, misread state); the site's content/design; a stand-in for a tool missing from your list — search for it instead.
CORE RULES:
- Only after a concrete observed failure. ONCE per distinct defect per session, then CONTINUE via a workaround if one exists.
- Truly blocked: `blockedTask=true`, tell the operator in one sentence what is blocked, stop that line of work (no retrying into the same wall).
- The result says where it went (this site only, or sent to the Caelo team) — tell the operator exactly that; never claim the team was notified unless it says sent.

title.description: The defect in a few words, e.g. "screenshot_page ignores selector".

whatHappened.description: Observed behaviour incl. the exact tool + arguments.

expected.description: What the tool description / system contract promised.

severity.description: blocking = no workaround | degraded = worked around | cosmetic = noise only.

blockedTask.description: true ONLY if you abandoned the current task because of this bug.

tools.name: get_site_defaults
tools.description: Fetch CURRENT site defaults + identity: default layout/template (slug + UUID), siteName, sitePurpose, siteLanguage (`<html lang>`), design brief. Read before set_site_defaults / set_site_identity, and after them for fresh state instead of repeating the write.

tools.name: list_pending_proposals
tools.description: List every proposal awaiting Owner approval across all gated domains (layouts, users, roles, reverts, themes, deploys, …). Call BEFORE queueing a proposal you may already have filed (duplicates are rejected) and after the user says they approved something. Rows with requestedBy=external-agent belong to an external MCP agent, which gets the decision and continues: in the Caelo chat do not act on or re-propose them.

tools.name: list_entity_locks
tools.description: List entities held by OTHER chat sessions (module/page/template/… + the holding chat). Held is not blocked: writing one ADOPTS that chat's unstaged change into this chat (nothing lost; your write builds on it; the result says so — tell the operator). Call before planning edits another chat may be working on, to say up front whose work you will take over. Every open chat's unstaged changes -> `list_unpublished_changes({allChats:true})`.

tools.name: list_users
tools.description: List site users (email, display name, roles); read-only. Changes: propose_create_user / propose_set_user_roles / propose_delete_user (Owner-approved). Re-call after an Owner approved one.

tools.name: list_roles
tools.description: List site roles (name, description, builtin); read-only. Changes: propose_create_role / propose_update_role_permissions / propose_delete_role (Owner-approved).

tools.name: list_ai_providers
tools.description: List configured AI providers (display name, active, key configured?, chat model, translation model + allowed catalogue models); never returns keys. Changes: propose_set_ai_provider / propose_clear_ai_provider_key; translation model: propose_set_translation_model (Owner-approved).

tools.name: list_domains
tools.description: List the site's domains (hostname, kind, TLS status). Changes -> `propose_add_domain`/`propose_remove_domain` (Owner-approved). Firebase Hosting installs also list each hosting custom domain's live state; 'stuck' -> `propose_reconnect_domain` heals it (CDN cache clears automatically once active).

tools.name: get_caelo_version
tools.description: Running Caelo version, newest release, update available (+ release-notes link). Use for version/update/release questions, or when a missing feature may need a newer Caelo. You cannot install updates — the Owner does at Settings → Updates (/settings/updates); say so and link it.

tools.name: list_caelo_updates
tools.description: Caelo update install history, newest first (version, who asked, outcome). Use for: did an update go through, why it failed, what changed recently. Current/newest version -> `get_caelo_version`.

tools.name: get_caelo_update
tools.description: Step-by-step timeline of one Caelo update install (signature check, backup, migrations, roll, health check, rollback); omit requestId = most recent (ids: `list_caelo_updates`). Use to explain what happened or why it stopped.

tools.name: get_caelo_update_policy
tools.description: Caelo auto-update policy: auto-install or notify only, which kinds (security, patch, minor; never major), maintenance window, soak periods, paused or not. Scheduler's last decision + update emails -> `get_caelo_auto_update_status`.

tools.name: get_caelo_update_agent
tools.description: Self-hosted only: is the server's update agent running (needed to install updates from Settings → Updates), or what is wrong (not set up, not running, cosign/Docker missing). Use when Install update is missing or an update didn't start.

tools.name: get_caelo_auto_update_status
tools.description: What the auto-update scheduler last decided about the newest release (installing, waiting for soak/window, paused, or why not) + update emails sent to the Owner and their delivery. Use for: will/when an update install by itself, why an update email did (not) arrive. Policy -> `get_caelo_update_policy`.

tools.name: add_module
tools.description:
Add ONE module to a page, a layout (site-wide chrome on every page) or a template (fans out to every page of that page type).
USE FOR: one incremental module on an existing page; chrome (`target:"layout"`); a module on every page of a template.
DO NOT USE FOR: a new page or a page needing >1 module -> `build_page` (whole ordered list WITH content, one transaction).
CORE RULES:
- Two modes, all targets. Reuse (check `list_modules` first): `moduleId` places a SHARED module without a duplicate; a later `update_modules_many` changes it everywhere. Placement-only: authoring fields passed alongside are NOT applied (result says so) — to change the module, place by `moduleId`, then `update_modules_many`. Mint: `html` + `displayName` + `kind` + `fields[]`.
- AUTHOR EXPLICITLY: pair `{{field_name}}` placeholders in `html` with explicit `fields[]` in semantic snake_case (`hero_title`, `primary_cta_href`, `nav_items`); never heuristic names (`cta2label2`, `spanText`).
- LISTS ARE LISTS: 10-item menu = ONE `list` field, never `label1`..`label10`; tag cloud = ONE `list` (`listType:"texts"`); multi-part items (image + heading + text) -> custom list type (`upsert_list_types_many`) or a `module-list` of a card module.
- Initial content comes IN THIS CALL via `values`. A mint with `fields` but neither `values` nor field defaults is REJECTED (would render empty placeholders).
- INTERNAL LINKS (`html` hrefs, `url`/`link` fields, list-entry links): write the page path (e.g. `/about`). Target MUST be an existing page (`list_pages`) or it is refused — create an empty shell first (`build_page({page:{slug, title}, modules:[]})`) or link after. `/` and `/#section` are always valid. Exception: links to pages of this chat's site-import run are kept and resolved by `resolve_import_links` at the end. Media/files: media URL (`find_media`). External: full `https://` URL.

Over this connection the install's AI is not used: the AI part comes back to you — a work item to answer with your own model and send back through the tool it names, or an `AiDelegated:` answer that says what to do instead (see caelo_get_context).

targetRef.description: Page: id or URL path (e.g. `/docs/setup`); a bare slug only while unique (nested pages can share slugs). Layout/template: slug or id.

blockName.description: Real block on the target; a mismatch error returns the valid set.

position.description: Integer as a bare number (`0`, not `"0"`).

html.description: Module HTML. Plain source (no CDATA or extra escaping). Placeholders: `{{field}}` primitives, `{{>field}}` single nested `module`, `{{#field}}…{{/field}}` `list` and `module-list`. Accordion, tabs, carousel, mobile-nav -> `data-caelo-ui` markup (see `js`) instead of custom JS.

css.description: Module CSS. Plain source (no CDATA or extra escaping). MUST scope every selector under the module's root class — bare selectors (`body`, `h1`, `.card`) bleed into other modules and are flagged.

js.description: Vanilla JS. Plain source (no CDATA or extra escaping). Emitted ONCE per page into a shared `

bindThemeLiterals.description: Rewrite CSS literals matching a theme token into `var(--…)`. Default true — omit unless keeping a deliberate off-palette literal.

default.description: ORIGINAL value(s) replaced (never a placeholder): scalar -> value; local `list` -> entries; shared `list` -> `"caelo:list/<id>"`. Omit for `module`, `module-list`, `bind:"source"`.

items.description: texts: `{node:"text", values:{text}}` | links: `{node:"link", values:{label, link:{href}}}` | menu: `{node:"entry", values:{label, link:{href}}, children}` | custom type: its fields (`list_list_types`). Keep `id` on resend.

node.description: NODE kind, not the listType slug: "text" (texts), "link" (links), "entry" (menu).

bind.description: For `kind:"list"`: `local` (default; entries live with the placement) | `shared` (site-wide menus/nav/footer/categories/tags — check `list_lists` first, edit entries via `patch_list_items_many`, share a local list via `promote_local_list`) | `source` (generated per page; placement content may set the knobs the source marks `editable`).

source.description: Required when `bind:"source"`: `{kind:"query", editable:[knobs], defaults:{page_type, terms, parent, order, limit}}` | `{kind:"system", name:"breadcrumbs"|"children"|"siblings"|"page_terms"|"term_pages"}` (only these) | `{kind:"plugin", name}` (e.g. `consent_categories`; iterating a plugin list needs no field).

allowedModuleTypes.description: For `module`/`module-list`: whitelist of stable module `type`s (e.g. `["button"]`), NOT slugs. Widen if a valid module is rejected.

values.description: Initial content `{field_name: value}` — the ONE place content goes. page/template: fills the placement(s). layout: stored as the minted module's field defaults (chrome has no content_instance) -> requires explicit `fields`; rejected with `moduleId` reuse (a shared module renders its stored defaults; change them via `update_modules_many`).

tools.name: add_plugin_to_page
tools.description: Place an active plugin's output (comments, contact form, ratings, newsletter signup …) on ONE page at a block + position, e.g. 'add comments to /about'. Active slugs: `list_plugins`. Site-wide (every blog post) = one call per page.

tools.name: create_template
tools.description:
Create a template (reusable HTML+CSS shell pages bind to) for a page type, e.g. 'a blog-post template'. NOT for a one-off page (`build_page`).
CORE RULES:
- A new KIND of content (news, products) is a page type first: `upsert_page_types_many` needs a template id -> create the template with its `pageType`, or create the type afterwards listing this template.
- `layoutId`: optional when a default layout exists (`get_site_defaults`; omitted -> that default); else REQUIRED, pick from `list_layouts` (omitting fails with 'no defaults'). Zero layouts -> `create_layout` first.
- Slots in `html` MUST be `<caelo-slot name="X"></caelo-slot>`, NOT comments like `<!-- block:X -->` (ignored -> page renders empty). Every block name needs a matching slot.

pageType.description: Page type slug (`list_page_types`); the template joins its templates. Omit = default page type.

blocks.description: Omit to auto-derive one block per `<caelo-slot>` (displayName = name); pass only for nicer displayNames or explicit positions.

tools.name: import_media_from_urls
tools.description:
Import source-site images, mp4 video and other assets into the media library by exact absolute URL (from `inspect_external_page`'s image inventory). THE way source media enters a migration — never `find_media` (Caelo library, empty then), never ask the operator to upload.
- Batch every asset a page needs in ONE call.
- Returns per asset the Caelo media URL (reference it in `build_page`) + mediaId (`set_theme_asset`/`set_media_alt_many`).
- The result lists every URL NOT imported (too large, fetch failed, blocked type): report it to the operator verbatim; never claim a clean import while it is non-empty.

name.description: Short human label from role/alt (logo -> "SearchVIU logo", hero -> "SearchVIU hero"). Becomes the PUBLIC media URL slug (`/_caelo/media/searchviu-logo`): name it like a human, not a filename. Omit only when the asset has no clear role.

tools.name: list_page_assets
tools.description: List EVERY asset URL (images, CSS backgrounds, video/audio/source) in a crawled import run's stored page HTML, ranked by frequency — the full inventory behind `inspect_external_page`'s top-20 `images`. Use when top-20 isn't enough or to find assets by URL across pages; then import via `import_media_from_urls`.

pageUrl.description: Only this crawled page (exact source URL).

tools.name: remove_module_from
tools.description: Remove a module reference from a page or layout; the module itself stays for reuse. `target:"page"` drops the page-level reference (any block); `target:"layout"` detaches site-wide chrome from every block of the layout ('remove the footer from every page'). To replace a module, PREFER `update_modules_many` (keeps the slot) over remove + add.

targetRef.description: Page: id or URL path (e.g. `/docs/setup`). Layout: slug or id.

tools.name: set_template_layout
tools.description: Re-point a template to another layout; its pages adopt the new chrome on next render (e.g. "make landing pages use the bare layout").

tools.name: create_layout
tools.description: Propose a layout (site shell) for a chrome variant no layout covers (e.g. campaign: banner, no footer). APPROVAL-GATED: only queues it for the Owner's click on the chat card; never claim it exists before. Then `set_template_layout` / `add_module` target='layout'.

html.description: Needs `<caelo-slot name="content"></caelo-slot>` + one slot per block.

tools.name: set_site_defaults
tools.description:
Set the site-wide default layout and/or template for new pages created without one. Safe to call directly: existing pages keep theirs.
CORE RULES: pass slugs (e.g. `site-default`), not UUIDs; current values via `get_site_defaults`, slugs via `list_layouts`/`list_templates`. FIRST set needs both fields, afterwards only the changed one. No layouts/templates yet -> `create_layout` -> `create_template` first.

tools.name: set_site_identity
tools.description:
Record the site identity so future chats inherit the brand context. `null` clears a field.
CORE RULES:
- Status note 'Site identity: not captured' -> call in your FIRST turn, inferring `siteName`, `sitePurpose`, `siteLanguage` from the operator's prompt, BEFORE authoring modules. E.g. 'homepage for an AI-first CMS called Caelo, trustworthy and developer-focused' -> `{siteName:'Caelo', sitePurpose:'An AI-first CMS for developers — trustworthy, branched edits, plugin sandbox', siteLanguage:'en'}`.
- Too little to infer (e.g. 'add a contact form' on an unconfigured install) -> ASK for the essentials, don't guess.

siteLanguage.description: BCP 47 language of the content (`en`, `de`, `pt-BR`), rendered as `<html lang>` on every page. No default: unset -> publishing fails, preview flags `site-language-unset`. Set it with the identity; infer from the operator's language / desired copy language or, when migrating, the `Lang:` from `inspect_external_page`; ask only if they disagree. Multilingual: the international-site plugin assigns translated pages their locale; this stays the language of unassigned pages.

designBrief.description: Pass during Site Genesis: feeds the parallel draft subagents and every future design decision.

tools.name: bootstrap_site_scaffold
tools.description:
Bootstrap a fresh install (layout + template + site defaults) — when the status note says 'needs setup' for them. Idempotent: each call detects and runs the next missing stage; the RESULT says which ran and what next.
- No layout: queues a layout PROPOSAL the operator approves on the chat's card. Don't claim it exists; after approval call this tool AGAIN.
- Layout exists: creates the template + pins site defaults directly. All exist: no-op.
All inputs optional; defaults = header/content/footer layout, single-block `home` template, pinned defaults.

tools.name: revert_chat_changes
tools.description:
Undo one chat's changes via ONE `propose_revert_site` proposal to the snapshot right before the chat started (one Owner click).
USE FOR: 'undo everything in this chat' / 'roll back session <id>'. Surgical rollback -> `propose_revert_page` / `propose_revert_module`.
WARNING: rewinds the FULL SITE — non-chat edits since then are reverted too. Refused when the chat is the site's first activity (no pre-chat snapshot) or touched more than `maxEntities` (default 20) entities.

tools.name: duplicate_page
tools.description: Clone a page under a new slug ('duplicate the about page'). Modules are shared by reference (edits hit both). The copy keeps the source's parent (`/docs/a` -> `/docs/<newSlug>`), page type, properties and terms (change later via `update_pages_many`); soft-deleted source modules are dropped. `targetTemplateId` of another page type -> the copy takes that type; block names must align, modules in unmatched blocks orphan -> fix with `repoint_page_template`.

newParentPageId.description: null = top level; omit = source's parent.

tools.name: set_home_page
tools.description: Make a page the site homepage, served at `/` (any page; keeps its own slug; no magic `home` slug). Exactly ONE homepage — replaces the previous one.

tools.name: set_not_found_page
tools.description:
Designate the site's 404 page (shown for every nonexistent URL).
USE WHEN the operator asks for an error/'page not found' page, or accepts your offer because the site status says no 404 page is designated (offer at the end of your turn; never build it unprompted inside another request).
CORE RULES:
- Build it like any page (`build_page`, the site's normal template so header/footer/theme apply; e.g. short 'Page not found' + links to homepage and main sections) -> PUBLISH (`set_pages_status_many`) -> call this with its id.
- Ships as /404.html with HTTP 404 for every unknown URL; NOT reachable at its own slug, noindex, not in the sitemap.
- ONE per site (replaces the previous); not the homepage.

pageId.description: null clears the designation (the hosting provider's generic error page returns).

tools.name: repoint_page_template
tools.description:
Re-point ONE page to another template with block migration: matching block names migrate; unmatched ones per `orphanDisposition`.
DO NOT USE FOR: >1 page to one template without block migration -> `update_pages_many`.
CORE RULES: modules would be dropped -> CONFIRM with the user before `{kind:"drop"}`. Relay the returned `migratedBlocks` + `droppedModules` in your reply.

tools.name: move_module
tools.description: Reposition a module on its page: into another block ('move the hero into the header', 'put this banner above the footer') or within its block ('move the testimonials above the gallery', 'put the hero last' — omit `toBlockName`). Already in place -> no-op.

toBlockName.description: Target block; omit to reorder within the current block.

position.description: 0-based index (clamped to the block end). `up`/`down` = one slot, current block only.

tools.name: find_media
tools.description: Search the EXISTING media library, most-used first, e.g. when the user describes an asset (TOON rows: id, name, mime, dims, alt, url). DO NOT USE FOR: site migrations (library is empty) -> `import_media_from_urls`. CORE RULES: `id` = media UUID for `set_theme_asset` / `set_media_alt_many` / `regenerate_media_variants`; take it from here, never invent one. `url` points at an EXISTING variant: use it verbatim in `` (via `update_modules_many`), never rewrite the variant segment. Reference images (generate/edit guides, not placeable) are hidden unless `visibility` is `reference` | `all`.

filter.description: Server-side search over alt text and filename.

tools.name: set_media_alt_many
tools.description: Replace alt text on assets (all-or-nothing) when you have visual context or an a11y request and the alt is missing/unhelpful. Never invent alt for an image you can't identify — omit that item. `assetId` = `id` from `find_media` or an `import_media_from_urls`/`generate_image` result.

tools.name: set_media_source_many
tools.description: Record assets' provenance (`sourceDetail` = source URL or AI provider/model) + licence (only one the operator states), all-or-nothing. Use after importing/generating media or when told a licence. Only passed fields change.

tools.name: set_media_visibility_many
tools.description: Mark media assets `reference` or `library` in one tx (ids from `find_media`).

visibility.description: `reference`: only guides image generation/editing (character sheet, style sample, product shot to match) — when the operator says so or uploads references; hidden from `find_media` (unless visibility "all"), a page using one fails its deploy. `library`: placeable on pages again (e.g. after a deploy error naming a reference image the operator wants published).

tools.name: regenerate_media_variants
tools.description:
Re-run the image pipeline for assets missing derived WebP variants; additive (existing variants untouched).
USE FOR: Stage/deploy fails with 'media references unresolved (asset/variant pairs missing)'. NOT for crops or layout resizes.
Result per asset: 'regenerated' lists new variants; 'skipped' = variant can NEVER exist (source narrower than breakpoint, animated GIF, non-raster) -> point the module HTML at the result's `bestUrl` (modules via `list_media_usages`), don't retry.

allMissing.description: Sweep every raster asset with an incomplete variant ladder instead.

tools.name: list_missing_media
tools.description:
List media assets whose stored files are gone (row exists, bytes lost). Use when Stage/deploy fails with 'stored files of … media asset(s) are missing', or before publishing after such a failure. Missing derived variants of an existing file -> `regenerate_media_variants`.
Per asset: `source` is a URL -> `import_media_from_urls` on it (same bytes refill the same asset, fixing every page); else ask the operator to re-upload the same file at /content/media (identical files reuse the asset). Unrestorable -> take it off its pages (`list_media_usages`), then `delete_media_many`.

tools.name: generate_image
tools.description: Generate a NEW image from a prompt with the configured image model; saved to the media library, returns mediaId + url (use the url verbatim in ``). EXISTING image -> `edit_image`. - Check `get_image_capabilities` first (reference count, sizes, resolutions); requests outside them are refused before anything is paid. - Rarely cheap: verify the prompt is on-brand. Budget reserved per call; `ImageBudgetExceeded` -> tell the operator, don't retry. Over this connection the install's AI is not used: the AI part comes back to you — a work item to answer with your own model and send back through the tool it names, or an `AiDelegated:` answer that says what to do instead (see caelo_get_context).

imageSize.description: 2K/4K only if `get_image_capabilities` lists them, else omit (1K works on every model).

references.description: Media ids/slugs (`find_media`, incl. `visibility:"reference"`) to keep a character, product or style consistent.

tools.name: edit_image
tools.description:
Edit an EXISTING library image by prompt ("make the sky dusk", "remove the logo") -> a NEW media asset linked to its source; the source is never modified. Brand-new image -> `generate_image`.
- Check `get_image_capabilities` first (edit support, mask support, reference limits); requests outside them are refused before anything is paid.
- Budget is reserved per call; `ImageBudgetExceeded` -> tell the operator, don't retry.

Over this connection the install's AI is not used: the AI part comes back to you — a work item to answer with your own model and send back through the tool it names, or an `AiDelegated:` answer that says what to do instead (see caelo_get_context).

mask.description: Library PNG whose transparent area marks what may change; mask-capable models only, else describe the region in `prompt`.

imageSize.description: 2K/4K only if `get_image_capabilities` lists them, else omit (1K works on every model).

tools.name: get_image_capabilities
tools.description: What the configured image model supports, read before `generate_image` / `edit_image`: operations, reference count + size/format limits, mask edits, output sizes, native resolutions, budget reserved per request. Free.

tools.name: set_page_seo_many
tools.description:
Set pages' SEO fields to exact values, all-or-nothing. ONLY on explicit user instruction (e.g. 'set the home meta description to X').
DO NOT USE FOR: first-publish fill -> `autofill_page_seo_many`; keyword re-optimization -> `bulk_optimize_seo`; side effect of content edits (never touch SEO then).

tools.name: autofill_page_seo_many
tools.description:
Write pages' FIRST meta description (+ optional og:image), one transaction. A Stage refuses pages without one -> run after building, before Staging.
DO NOT USE FOR: pages created with `build_page` -> pass `page.metaDescription` there; changing a filled description -> `bulk_optimize_seo` (only when the user asks) or `set_page_seo_many` (exact user-dictated value).
CORE RULES:
- Write each from the page's actual content, 150–160 chars for a human reading a search result: read core texts with ONE `get_page_seo({pageIds})`, never by rendering; or carry over the source description when migrating. Title 50–60 chars via `update_pages_many`.
- Fill-once: same text again = no-op; a DIFFERENT text for a filled page (AlreadyAutofilled) aborts the whole batch -> leave such pages out.

tools.name: find_redirects
tools.description: Search redirects (TOON rows: fromPath, toPath, status). Pre-flight before `bulk_delete_redirects` so the user sees what goes.

filter.description: Substring of fromPath / toPath, searched across the whole table.

tools.name: check_links
tools.description:
Check internal links (to own pages/media) in your draft, wherever stored: page content, module HTML, field defaults, layouts, templates, lists (menus, vocabularies), page terms/properties, plugin data. Each problem names the page, storage place and fixing tool.
Severity: BLOCK Stage + Publish = links to deleted pages/media, links without a page in the linking page's language, refs to a deleted list, removed term or deleted module in a list entry. BLOCK Publish (Stage warning) = links to unpublished pages. Warning = old plain-path links.
USE FOR: before `stage_changes` after deleting/unpublishing/translating pages; a Stage refused for links; operator asks about broken links.
DO NOT USE FOR: external links or the built site (`get_quality_audit` checks the staged build).

for.description: Gate: 'publish' (default; Publish live / promote) -> a link to an unpublished page blocks; 'stage' -> only a warning.

pagePath.description: Only this page's problems (path, e.g. '/about'); site-wide places (menus, plugin data) always included.

tools.name: get_quality_audit
tools.description:
Read the staged site's quality check: plugin page checks (when an active plugin adds any, e.g. SEO) reading EVERY page on every Stage, plus a mobile Lighthouse audit (Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, SEO) when the Stage changed how pages render. No args = newest audit of THIS chat's Stages.
Returns per page: scores; Performance metrics (FCP, LCP, TBT, CLS, Speed Index: best run + Lighthouse rating; LCP element + breakdown; shifted elements + causes); each problem's Lighthouse audit id (e.g. `image-alt`, `color-contrast`, `render-blocking-insight`) + flagged elements (selector, HTML snippet, why, e.g. measured contrast); each page-check problem's rule id `<check>/<rule>` (contains a slash, e.g. `seo-check/title-missing`) + fix hint naming the tool. Plus site-wide findings, non-blocking warnings/hints, infrastructure errors.
USE FOR: after a Stage, what to fix. Already accepted -> `list_quality_acceptances`. Never run Lighthouse yourself: the audit runs on the real staged build (no other URL serves it).
CORE RULES:
- TARGET 100 IN EVERY CATEGORY + ZERO FINDINGS: every category <100, every scored Lighthouse audit below perfect, every page-check error BLOCKS Publish live. 90 is NOT acceptable — fix until 100 wherever achievable. ACCEPTED problems don't block (a worse value than accepted blocks again). Warnings/hints never block.
- Speed: fix the worst metric in the module rendering the named element, Stage again, re-read — repeat until Performance 100.
- Only the truly unfixable goes to the operator: one decision per group (`accept_quality_findings` with `groups`) + the reason.
- CAELO PLATFORM findings (back/forward cache, caching of Caelo's own files, server response, compression, redirects) come from Caelo's hosting/build: report via `bug_report`, never edit the site for them; they block until Caelo fixes it or the operator accepts.
- Without an open operator chat (Power-MCP) a call on a queued/running audit waits up to ~50 s; call again if still running.

deployRunId.description: The newest audit of this staging deploy run.

pageId.description: Only this page's section (id from `list_pages`); run summary + site-wide checks stay.

tools.name: check_stage_audit
tools.description: Before suggesting a Stage: will THIS chat's pending changes trigger a Lighthouse audit, and why? (Active plugin page checks read every page on EVERY Stage regardless.) Lighthouse runs for new/changed module html/css/js, layout/template/theme changes, new pages, plugin config — not for only text/field values, placing/moving existing modules, SEO texts, redirects. Returns the deciding changes, covered pages, and last Performance metrics (FCP, LCP, TBT, CLS, Speed Index; LCP element, layout shifts) of those pages + homepage — the start for a speed fix (target Performance 100). Never run Lighthouse yourself: the audit runs on the real staged build.

tools.name: list_quality_audits
tools.description: List recent quality audits of staging deploys, newest first. Find an audit id for `get_quality_audit` or check whether the last Stage's audit still runs.

tools.name: list_quality_acceptances
tools.description: List accepted quality findings, category scores <100 and page-check rules. Check before asking the operator to decide something again. An acceptance applies ONLY to its page (`site-wide` = site-wide page-check rule). It records the accepted value — `score`: category score; `finding`: audit score in points (acceptedScore); `check`: up to acceptedCount errors of its rule (auditId = rule id); a worse value blocks again. `filter` searches audit/rule id, reason, page path.

tools.name: get_publish_gate
tools.description: Is Publish live open for the staged build? If not: why + next step (fix quality problems — target 100, zero findings — or hand truly unfixable ones to the operator as a decision; retry a failed check; wait for a running one). Call before telling the operator they can publish. Findings -> `get_quality_audit`.

tools.name: retry_quality_audit
tools.description: Re-run the staged build's quality check when it FAILED (browser, timeout, staging unreachable) or never ran; changes nothing. Not for re-checking fixes — those need a new Stage, which audits itself.

tools.name: accept_quality_findings
tools.description:
Hand the operator a decision on quality findings that truly CANNOT be fixed, or record an acceptance they explicitly asked for ("accept it", "ship it anyway").
CORE RULES:
- Target = 100 per Lighthouse category + zero findings; 90 is NOT acceptable on its own. Fix what is fixable (metrics: `get_quality_audit`; never run Lighthouse yourself).
- On your own only after explaining WHY it cannot be fixed (third-party embed, brand colour the operator confirmed, Caelo platform issue reported via `bug_report`); phrase it as the operator's choice, never your recommendation.
- Check `list_quality_acceptances` first; never ask twice. Every group of one decision -> ONE call.
- Accepts the value measured now (score, audit score, error count): worse blocks again, better tightens it. Applies ONLY to its pages.
- Once approved it counts at once — Publish live opens without a new Stage. Do NOT call `stage_changes` to 'pick it up': a Stage with nothing new re-runs the whole check and can start another fix round.
APPROVAL-GATED: pauses for the operator's in-chat Approve/Reject before anything changes; do not claim it is live until approved.

Over MCP: call this tool yourself — it works here. The call queues an approval card in the operator's Caelo admin (their Live Edit chat and the pending-approvals page), waits for their Approve/Reject and returns the outcome (if the wait times out, continue with caelo_await_approval). Tell the operator you requested it and that they approve the card in Caelo; never ask them to paste a prompt into the Caelo chat to run it.

auditRunId.description: From `get_quality_audit` (as are page paths and audit/rule ids).

items.description: Only for single findings on named pages.

groups.description: PREFERRED: one problem across pages per entry. `{ruleId:"seo-check/description-missing"}` = every page it is open on; `pagePaths` = subset; Lighthouse audit by `auditId`, category below 100 by `category`.

reason.description: The operator's reason, or the plain fact why it cannot be fixed.

tools.name: publish_despite_failed_audit
tools.description:
Publish the staged build live although its quality check FAILED to run (not when it found problems), recording the editor's reason. ONLY on the editor's explicit request, after `retry_quality_audit`. auditRunId: `get_publish_gate`.
APPROVAL-GATED: pauses for the operator's in-chat Approve/Reject before anything changes; do not claim it is live until approved.

Over MCP: call this tool yourself — it works here. The call queues an approval card in the operator's Caelo admin (their Live Edit chat and the pending-approvals page), waits for their Approve/Reject and returns the outcome (if the wait times out, continue with caelo_await_approval). Tell the operator you requested it and that they approve the card in Caelo; never ask them to paste a prompt into the Caelo chat to run it.

tools.name: inspect_page_render
tools.description:
Inspect a rendered page's HTML/CSS cascade; default = slim summary (modules with moduleId/slug/kind/sizes, layer sizes, slot status).
USE FOR: the actual rule behind a layout/CSS issue a screenshot can't explain.
DO NOT USE FOR: the visual impression -> `screenshot_page`.
Renders this chat's branch preview (pending edits included); outside a chat -> published version.

chatBranchId.description: Omit (= this chat's branch). Only for another branch the operator may see: shared draft or their own chats; other editors' experiments -> 'branch not found'.

target.description: Omit = summary. `composed` (final HTML) | `layout` | `template` | `theme` (that layer's html+css / tokens) | a moduleId from the summary (its html+css).

search.description: Grep the composed HTML: returns only matching slices with context (cheaper than the whole document).

tools.name: inspect_built_page
tools.description: Read a page's BUILT HTML from the staging or production bucket — use AFTER Stage to verify the build. Catches what the preview can't show: missing SEO meta, hashed-asset URLs, plugin render transforms, CSP-relevant `<script src>`, robots.txt overrides.

runId.description: Pin a staging run; default latest succeeded.

tools.name: screenshot_page
tools.description:
Screenshot a rendered Caelo page of this chat's branch preview (pending edits included). The image returns WITHIN this turn — analyse it next step, do NOT end the turn to wait; not persisted across the chat.
USE FOR: gross visual impression (crowded hero? colors/imagery? overall layout?).
DO NOT USE FOR: spacing/layout/CSS questions (word gaps, flex stacking, white halo around the header, wrong colors, broken layout) -> `inspect_page_render` (summary, then `target`/`search`: composed HTML + each CSS layer, the source of truth).
CORE RULES:
- ALWAYS call after composing a page or structural/styling changes — desktop AND mobile — and fix real issues BEFORE telling the operator you're done (max two review rounds; skip for content-only edits).
- Backend: interactive chat -> operator's browser (html2canvas, their exact viewport); no attached browser (MCP, background sends, subagents) -> real headless Chromium on the server. Result names the backend.
- html2canvas is an APPROXIMATION that mis-renders (1) fine text spacing (irregular word gaps like broken justify) and (2) flex-wrap (one item per line).
