Artifacts, NOT CSS bugs: never edit CSS or file a bug from a browser-captured screenshot alone — confirm with `inspect_page_render`. Chromium renders have no such artifacts.

chatBranchId.description: Omit (defaults to this chat's branch). Set only for another branch: the shared draft or the operator's own chats' branches; other editors' experiments -> 'branch not found'.

viewport.description: desktop (default) = operator's live preview size in interactive chat (result states size + whose view), else 1280x800; tablet = 768x1024; mobile = 375x812.

width.description: Overrides the viewport width (CSS px; height unchanged). Omit on the first capture (= operator's view). Desktop is not one width: vw/clamp() type wraps differently (3 lines at 1280px, 4 at 1740px) -> for typography/layout reviews ALSO capture a second width (1280 if the operator's view is wider, 1920 if narrower); the design must hold at both. Operator reports a wrap/break you don't see -> re-capture without `width` before concluding it's fine.

selector.description: CSS selector: capture only the first match (e.g. '[data-caelo-module-id="<uuid>"]', 'footer.caelo-layout-footer') — cheaper when checking one module. Error if nothing matches.

tools.name: bulk_create_redirects
tools.description: Create redirects in one tx: a single one, a list ('/old-blog/* -> /blog/*' across many paths), a pasted CSV/table. `upsert:true` updates existing fromPath rows instead of skipping them.

toPath.description: Path on this site, single leading '/' (e.g. '/blog/new'); never a full URL or '//host' (external targets unsupported).

tools.name: bulk_delete_redirects
tools.description:
Delete redirects in one transaction by EXACTLY ONE of `redirectIds`, `fromPaths`, `matches` (one redirect = one-item array). Run `find_redirects` FIRST and tell the user the count.
`matches` (substring) is capped at 10 rows for you (every deleted 301 strands an inbound link): more -> REJECTED, nothing deleted; list them with `find_redirects`, show the operator, delete the confirmed ones by `redirectIds` (uncapped).

tools.name: bulk_optimize_seo
tools.description:
Re-optimize meta descriptions (+ og:image) of 1..N pages, all-or-nothing, regardless of fill state.
USE FOR: ONLY an explicit user request to optimize/rewrite SEO with context (keywords, intent, branding).
DO NOT USE FOR: first-publish fill -> `autofill_page_seo_many`; exact dictated value -> `set_page_seo_many`.
First read current descriptions + core text with ONE `get_page_seo({pageIds})`.

context.description: The user's brief, applied to every item.

tools.name: delete_pages_many
tools.description:
Soft-delete 1..N pages — the ONLY page delete tool.
CORE RULES:
- Each item's `disposition` handles its dead URL: ALWAYS confirm it with the operator; for `redirect` suggest a target (parent section, sibling, `/`). Items may differ.
- A page with child pages is refused unless the call also deletes all of them or the item sets `children` — ask the operator which when unclear.
- 5+ pages (subtrees counted) pause for one Owner click in chat before running.
- One snapshot per page (undo: `propose_revert_site` / `propose_revert_page`). Result: deleted/alreadyDeleted/notFound counts + each refused page with reason.

Over MCP: when this call needs the operator's approval, it queues an approval card in their Caelo admin (Live Edit chat and the pending-approvals page) and returns the outcome once they decide — tell them to approve the card; never ask them to paste a prompt into the Caelo chat.

redirectTo.description: Required for `redirect`: on-site path with one leading `/` (e.g. `/blog`); never a full URL or `//host`.

children.description: Page with child pages: `move-up` -> to this page's parent (old URLs 301) | `delete` -> whole subtree, same disposition.

tools.name: update_pages_many
tools.description:
Edit metadata of 1..N pages — the ONLY tool for it: rename, retitle, reslug, status, template, page type, properties, terms.
DO NOT USE FOR: nesting under another page / back to top level -> `move_pages`; SEO -> `set_page_seo_many`; modules -> `update_modules_many`.
CORE RULES:
- THREE independent identifiers, never substitute one for another: `name`, `title`, `slug`. Operator says only 'rename' -> ASK which (usually `name`).
- Changing `slug` moves the page's URL AND every nested page's URL; a 301 from each old URL is created in the same transaction. On-site links (menus, link lists, modules, content) follow automatically — do not update them. A slug change moving 10+ URLs (page + subtree) pauses for one Owner click in chat.
- Items apply independently: per-item failures (not found, version conflict) are reported, the rest applies.

Over MCP: when this call needs the operator's approval, it queues an approval card in their Caelo admin (Live Edit chat and the pending-approvals page) and returns the outcome once they decide — tell them to approve the card; never ask them to paste a prompt into the Caelo chat.

name.description: Internal editor label (page picker / breadcrumbs); not public.

pageType.description: What the page IS (`list_page_types` slug, e.g. `news`); page queries ('latest news', 'articles in this category') filter on type/properties/terms. Template must be one of the type's templates, else pass `templateId` too.

properties.description: Page type properties, merged (null removes one), e.g. `{author:'Ada', event_date:'2026-11-03'}`.

terms.description: REPLACES the page's terms, from the page type's vocabularies (categories, tags; `get_list` shows entry ids). `[]` clears.

redirectFromOld.description: Only with `slug`. `skip` = no 301 — ONLY when the operator explicitly wants the old URL to 404.

tools.name: move_pages
tools.description:
Nest pages under other pages or back to top level, 1..N moves in one transaction ('put Alerts under SEO Monitoring').
DO NOT USE FOR: only renaming name/title/slug -> `update_pages_many`; new page under a parent -> `build_page` with `page.parentPageId`.
CORE RULES: URL = parent URL + '/' + slug; subpages move along. 301s from old URLs are automatic; on-site links follow on their own (no link-update step). Target URL taken -> nothing changes, clash named -> retry with `newSlug`. Homepage can't move under a page or have children; max 6 levels. 10+ moved URLs (incl. subtrees) pause for one Owner click in chat.

Over MCP: when this call needs the operator's approval, it queues an approval card in their Caelo admin (Live Edit chat and the pending-approvals page) and returns the outcome once they decide — tell them to approve the card; never ask them to paste a prompt into the Caelo chat.

parent.description: Id or URL path; null = top level.

newSlug.description: Rename in the same step; needed when the target URL is taken.

redirectFromOld.description: 'skip' = no 301s; only when the operator wants old URLs to 404.

tools.name: update_modules_many
tools.description:
Edit module structure (`html`, `fields`, `css`, `js`, `displayName`, `description`, `kind`, `type`) of 1..N modules. Every page using a module follows; chat-branched until publish.
USE FOR: wholesale rewrites, new module bodies, changes to `fields`/`displayName`/`kind`/`type`/`description`, the same fix across modules.
DO NOT USE FOR: a TARGETED change to existing `html`/`css`/`js` -> PREFER `edit_content` (surgical string-replace: cheaper, reviewable diff); page/instance content -> `set_page_module_content_many` (per page) | `set_content_instance_values_many` (shared); page metadata -> `update_pages_many`; templates -> `propose_update_template`.
CORE RULES:
- AUTHOR EXPLICITLY: pair `{{field_name}}` placeholders in `html` with explicit `fields[]` in semantic snake_case (`hero_title`, `primary_cta_href`, `nav_items`); never heuristic names (`cta2label2`, `spanText`).
- LISTS ARE LISTS: 10-item menu = ONE `list` field, never `label1`..`label10`; tag cloud = ONE `list` (`listType:"texts"`); multi-part items (image + heading + text) -> custom list type (`upsert_list_types_many`) or a `module-list` of a card module.
- KEEP METADATA FRESH: update `description` + `kind` when a module's purpose drifts (`list_modules` relies on them).
- Items apply independently: a failed item (not found, draft conflict, invalid field) is reported with its reason, the rest commits; nothing updated -> error. One snapshot per module.
- INTERNAL LINKS (`html` hrefs, `url`/`link` fields, list-entry links): write the page path (e.g. `/about`). Target MUST be an existing page (`list_pages`) or it is refused — create an empty shell first (`build_page({page:{slug, title}, modules:[]})`) or link after. `/` and `/#section` are always valid. tools.name: set_theme_tokens
tools.description:
Update tokens of one theme: upsert per token (a complete replacement = pass every desired token); names are normalized to canonical paths and the result shows what was written.
DO NOT USE FOR: a new theme -> `propose_create_theme`.

fontBindings.description: Pin exact font files per role (e.g. `body`, `heading`) with `{id, sha256}` from `find_fonts`/`acquire_font`.

fontAxes.description: Which part of a pinned VARIABLE font visitors download, per role, e.g. `{heading:{opsz:"full"}}`, `{body:{wght:{min:400,max:700}}}`; `null` resets a role. Per axis: "full" = whole range | `{min,max}` clamps | number pins. Policy belongs to the font FILE -> applies to every role using it. Default (usually right): wght clamped to the weights the site renders, other axes pinned to the font default (~halves Inter's download). Trade-offs: pinned opsz renders large headings in the text optical size (heavier, less refined) -> `{opsz:"full"}` to keep optical sizes; a wght range excluding a used weight renders that text at the nearest kept weight. Read current policy + byte sizes first via `get_theme(as:"font-delivery")`. Axes/values the font lacks are rejected with its real ranges.

set.description: Add/replace tokens by loose name (`primaryColor`, `fontHeading`, `spacingLg`) or canonical path; value rules under `tokens`. Ambiguous bare name -> `UnknownTokenName` with did-you-mean -> retry with the canonical path.

tokens.description: (Partial) DTCG document in the `get_theme`/`propose_create_theme` shape (`{color:{primary:{$value:'#4338ca', $description:'…'}}, typography:{…}}`); every `{$value}` leaf is upserted at its path -> a whole composed palette in one call. Rules for values via `tokens` or `set`: Composite shapes (copy exactly): typography leaf = `{$type: 'typography', $value: {fontFamily: 'Inter, sans-serif', fontSize: '1rem', fontWeight: 400, lineHeight: 1.6}}`, one composite per body/heading/mono (never per-property tokens; fontFamily a plain string). Shadow leaf = `{$type: 'shadow', $value: {color: '#0b132b33', offsetX: '0px', offsetY: '2px', blur: '8px', spread: '0px'}}`, an object or array of them, never a raw CSS string. Gradient leaf = a CSS `linear-` / `radial-` / `conic-gradient(...)` string (not a color) under `gradient.*`, `$type` inferred: `set: {'gradient.hero': {$type: 'gradient', $value: 'linear-gradient(135deg, #4f46e5, #7c3aed)'}}` (the bare string or a `*Gradient` name also routes to a gradient token). Never alias ({group.token}) unless the target exists. `spacing` must cover what pages use, or module CSS falls back to literals the operator cannot retune: component steps `xs`…`2xl` (0.25-3rem; controls need 0.6-0.9rem padding) PLUS rhythm tokens `section-sm` (~2.5rem tight band), `section` (~4rem standard band), `section-lg` (~5rem hero / feature band). Module CSS references them (`padding: var(--spacing-section) var(--spacing-md)`); about to write a padding literal -> add the token instead. Record each token's ROLE in `$description`: with the value (`set: {'color.primary': {$type: 'color', $value: '#4f46e5', $description: 'CTAs, links and selected states — never large background fills'}}`) or as a value-less patch on a settled value (`set: {'color.primary': {$description: '…'}}` leaves `$value` untouched; needs the canonical path or the `--css-var` name, since a loose name infers its category from the value). Say where it must NOT be used, not only where. Roles survive value-only edits and every module write replays the roles of the vars its CSS touches: this is the whole design-system record, no separate manifest. Typography by role: body = sustained reading, heading = hierarchy and navigation, optional `typography.display` composite for expressive hero / campaign titles. Real, resolvable families and supported numeric weights; one or two complementary families unless the brand needs more. A display title needs deliberate size, line breaks, weight, spacing and composition, not an enlarged or rainbow-colored body font. Record use and exclusions in each token's $description; reference --font-display, --text-display, --font-weight-display and --tracking-display only after creating those tokens. Keep established brand typography unless the operator asks for a redesign. Preview the actual rendered fonts with the operator's text (accents, non-Latin characters): a family name in a picker does not prove its face loaded. Check mobile line breaks and reading contrast. Use the self-hosted font resolver and surface unresolved families; no external font links. AI-generated lettering is a separate image asset, never a reusable font or editable text: only on explicit request, verify exact spelling, keep accessible semantic text without a duplicate visible title. Web-font availability does not establish PDF embedding support.

Keep established brand typography unless the operator asks for a redesign. Preview the actual rendered fonts with the operator's text (accents, non-Latin characters): a family name in a picker does not prove its face loaded. Check mobile line breaks and reading contrast. Use the self-hosted font resolver and surface unresolved families; no external font links. AI-generated lettering is a separate image asset, never a reusable font or editable text: only on explicit request, verify exact spelling, keep accessible semantic text without a duplicate visible title. Web-font availability does not establish PDF embedding support.

overrides.description: `primaryColor` -> server derives a 50–900 OKLCh lightness ramp (stops marked `_derived: true`); explicit stops (`"color.primary.500": '#…'`) win.

tools.name: propose_activate_theme
tools.description:
Switch the site's active theme. Approval flips the DB row only; the live site keeps the old theme's CSS until `propose_deploy_promote` is also approved: tell the operator both steps are needed.
APPROVAL-GATED: pauses for the operator's in-chat Approve/Reject before anything changes; do not claim it is live until approved.

tools.name: propose_delete_theme
tools.description:
Delete an inactive theme (the active one is rejected: `propose_activate_theme` another first).
APPROVAL-GATED: pauses for the operator's in-chat Approve/Reject before anything changes; do not claim it is live until approved.

Tell the operator you requested it and that they approve the card in Caelo; never ask them to paste a prompt into the Caelo chat to run it.

tools.name: deploy_staging
tools.description:
Rebuild the STAGING site (noindex, never visitor-facing) from PUBLISHED content; returns run id, page/file counts, preview URL.
USE FOR: before `propose_deploy_promote` when staging has no (or an outdated) successful build | after fixing a failed build (e.g. `regenerate_media_variants`) | operator asks to refresh staging.
CORE RULES: this chat's unpublished changes are NOT in the build until published; never tell the operator pending edits are on staging. Production isn't reachable here: go live via `propose_deploy_promote`. Failed build -> fix the generator's named cause, then call again; never retry unchanged.

targetName.description: Omit when the site has one staging target (usual).

tools.name: verify_domains
tools.description:
Check whether registered domains resolve (A/AAAA); refreshes verification stamp + provisional TLS status. Read-only.
USE FOR: after DNS changes, an approved `propose_add_domain`, or TLS 'unknown'/'pending' in `list_domains`.
DO NOT USE FOR: exact installer records (CNAME/TXT values) -> `verify_dns_records`.
'stuck' (Firebase Hosting) -> `propose_reconnect_domain`. 'not resolved' = usually still propagating (minutes-hours): report it, don't retry in a loop.

hostnames.description: As shown by `list_domains`. Omit for all.

tools.name: verify_dns_records
tools.description:
Check DNS records carry the expected value: ok | pending (unpublished/propagating) | mismatch (other value). Read-only.
USE FOR: site or certificate not coming up; after the operator changed DNS.
DO NOT USE FOR: a quick 'does it resolve' check of registered domains -> `verify_domains`.

records.description: Omit (usual) = every record the installer stored as required (site/admin A|CNAME, certificate TXT); result names each record's purpose -> tell the operator what to add/fix at the registrar. Explicit records only on the site's own domains (registered, base-URL host, installer records, their subdomains).

environment.description: With `records` omitted: only this environment's records.

tools.name: delete_media_many
tools.description:
Delete media assets the site no longer uses (library clean-up, e.g. unused stock photos, duplicate logos). Irreversible from chat.
DO NOT USE FOR: keeping an asset but hiding it from page placement -> `set_media_visibility_many` (`reference`).
CORE RULES: assets still embedded in a module (live or in this chat's unpublished edits) are NOT deleted — returned as blocked with their modules. Remove the image there first (`update_modules_many` / `set_page_module_content_many`) or tell the operator it is in use; no force option.

tools.name: delete_modules_many
tools.description: Delete modules no longer placed anywhere (cleanup after a redesign/migration). A still-placed module is refused (not deleted) and the result names where it is used: unplace via `remove_module_from` first, or keep it. Lands on the chat preview, live on publish; Undo restores. To take a module off one page but keep it -> `remove_module_from`.

moduleIds.description: From `list_modules` (its usage column shows unplaced ones).

tools.name: accept_import_pages
tools.description:
Take crawled pages over AS-IS: each becomes a DRAFT page (chat preview, nothing published) from the crawl's content blocks (header/footer excluded — layout owns chrome), linked to its import row. All-or-nothing.
USE FOR: verbatim import ('bring the blog posts over as they are').
DO NOT USE FOR: a faithful rebuild in the site's design -> `build_page` with `page.importPageId` (the normal migration path).
Already accepted/built pages are refused (edit that page). Template block names must match the crawl's, else the call fails naming the block -> pick another template.

templateId.description: From `list_templates`; omit for the site default.

tools.name: cleanup_import_run
tools.description:
Close a finished site-import run and permanently delete crawl data (staging rows + screenshots) of pages never accepted or built; built pages stay.
USE only when the operator says the migration is done and the leftover crawl can go. Irreversible: `get_import_page`/`list_import_pages` lose the dropped pages and a re-crawl costs time + money -> build still-needed pages first.
APPROVAL-GATED: your call queues it; data is deleted only after the operator clicks Approve on the in-chat card. Do not claim cleanup before that.

Over MCP: when this call needs the operator's approval, it queues an approval card in their Caelo admin (Live Edit chat and the pending-approvals page) and returns the outcome once they decide — tell them to approve the card; never ask them to paste a prompt into the Caelo chat.

tools.name: resolve_import_links
tools.description: Finish an import-run rebuild's links. During the rebuild, links to the run's pages (crawled, in the run's URL list, or linked from crawled pages) are kept as written and recorded instead of refused; other unknown paths are still refused. Call ONCE when every run page is built (before `get_import_run_report`): rewrites recorded links to now-existing pages and lists still-unmatched links with locations -> fix each (build the page or point at an existing path), call again. Safe to repeat; run cleanup does it too. Not for links outside an import (checked on write).

tools.name: send_test_email
tools.description: Send the fixed 'Caelo email transport test' message (no custom mail) via the configured transport; reports whether the provider accepted it. Use after an approved `propose_set_email_config`, or when reset/form emails don't arrive. A failure names the provider's reason (bad API key, unverified sender domain, transport 'none') — relay it, don't retry unchanged.

to.description: Must be on the sender's (fromAddress) domain (sender noreply@example.com -> team@example.com ok); other addresses -> tell the operator to test from Settings -> Email.

tools.name: get_ai_spend
tools.description: Report AI spend over a window: total cost + tokens, text vs image, per provider/model, per source (plugin, person, subagent), recent days, admin domains the AI's tool calls hit (op counts + failures). Use for what AI costs, why a budget warned, which feature is expensive. Caps -> `get_ai_budgets`; one plugin vs its cap -> `get_plugin`.

tools.name: get_plugin
tools.description:
Read one plugin in detail: version, tier, status, signature, health (loaded on the running servers? why not), recent errors, validator findings, declared tools/skills/capabilities, AI spend last 24h vs its cap. Never returns source.
USE FOR: when `list_plugins`' summary isn't enough: why it fails or a submission was rejected, what an inactive plugin adds before `activate_plugin`, whether it nears its AI cap.
Errors: `core` = Caelo's fault; its line says whether the bug report was only recorded on this site or sent to the Caelo team -> repeat exactly, never say the team knows unless it says sent | `plugin` = the plugin's own code | `transient` = retried. Errors never switch a plugin off.

tools.name: get_gateway_analytics
tools.description: Public API gateway traffic (visitor writes to plugin endpoints: forms, comments, signups) over a rolling window: requests, p95 latency, errors, throttled + honeypot-caught counts, overall and for the busiest (plugin, operation) pairs. Use when a form may be spammed or an endpoint slow, and before `tune_rate_limit`. Individual requests -> `list_gateway_requests`.

tools.name: list_gateway_requests
tools.description: List recent public API gateway requests, newest first: plugin, operation, status, duration, body size, rate-limited/honeypot/captcha. Diagnose a failing or abused endpoint; totals -> `get_gateway_analytics`.

tools.name: list_rate_limit_profiles
tools.description: List named rate-limit profiles (per-visitor max per window) + how many plugin endpoints use each. Read before `tune_rate_limit` so the proposal fits the limits in use.

tools.name: get_email_config
tools.description: Read the site's email setup: transport, from-address, settings. Set credentials read "[redacted]" (you see THAT a key exists, never the key). Use before `propose_set_email_config`, or when a form/newsletter mail didn't arrive (then `send_test_email` checks delivery).

tools.name: list_bug_reports
tools.description: List defect reports filed against Caelo (via `bug_report` or auto-captured by the chat), newest first. Call BEFORE `bug_report` to see whether it is already reported. Forwarding column: local_only = this site only, the Caelo team has NOT seen it | queued = will be sent | sent = the team received it | failed = sending failed, stored here only. local_only/failed reach the team only when the Owner clicks "Send unsent reports" on Settings → Detected bugs (sending turned on); you cannot send them. Never tell the operator the team knows unless forwarding is sent.

tools.name: get_media_settings
tools.description: Read media CDN settings: whether heavily used images are copied to the CDN, from which usage count. Changing them = Owner decision (billing) at /settings/media.

tools.name: list_snapshots
tools.description: List edit history (snapshots), newest first: id, time, change kind, entities touched. USE FOR: the snapshotId a `propose_revert_*` needs; 'what changed here lately?'. Inspect one -> `get_snapshot`.

tools.name: get_snapshot
tools.description: Inspect one snapshot: description, author, chat + recorded state per touched entity (truncated). Use before a revert proposal to confirm it holds the version meant. Ids: `list_snapshots`.

tools.name: get_module_impact
tools.description: Blast radius of editing one module: every live page placing it + severity and reasons. Use BEFORE editing a possibly shared module (header, footer, CTA) to tell the operator what else changes, or to pick `fork_placement_content` instead.

tools.name: list_unpublished_changes
tools.description: List what THIS chat changed that is not published yet (pages, modules, templates, layouts, theme, lists), split unstaged | staged. Use before saying work is ready to publish, to summarise what publishing ships, or to check an edit landed.

allChats.description: true = EVERY open chat's unstaged changes + held entities (all editors): what is open across chats, or before touching something another chat may hold.

tools.name: stage_changes
tools.description:
Stage: merge this chat's unstaged changes into the site, rebuild the STAGING site (noindex, never visitor-facing), then run the quality check (Lighthouse). Use when the requested change is done and should be reviewed: 'stage it', 'put it on staging', last step of finished work.
CORE RULES:
- Other chats' changes to the SAME module/page ride along (result names them -> tell the operator).
- Only status 'published' pages are built; result lists left-out drafts -> `set_pages_status_many` first if they belong on staging.
- REFUSED unless: (1) >=1 published page; (2) a published page serves '/' (`set_home_page`, slug kept); (3) every published page has a meta description (`page.metaDescription` in `build_page`, else ONE `autofill_page_seo_many` call). Covers untouched pages too; the turn-start status note and results of `build_page` / `set_pages_status_many` / `set_home_page` / `autofill_page_seo_many` say 'A Stage would be refused right now' + exact fixes -> do them first, then stage once.
- Does NOT publish: Publish live = operator's click after the check (`get_publish_gate` open?, `get_quality_audit` findings). Never say the change is live.
- Failed build returns the generator's error -> fix, retry; changes stay unstaged until a build succeeds.

scope.description: `all_my_chats` = every open chat of the operator with unstaged changes, one build.

tools.name: undo_this_chat
tools.description:
Undo THIS chat's unstaged changes in the shared draft (since its last Stage) — 'undo that', 'throw this away', 'go back to before this chat'. Staged/published changes -> `propose_revert_*`. Chats on their own experiment/migration branch are discarded from Open changes instead.

Over MCP: when this call needs the operator's approval, it queues an approval card in their Caelo admin (Live Edit chat and the pending-approvals page) and returns the outcome once they decide — tell them to approve the card; never ask them to paste a prompt into the Caelo chat.

confirmOverlap.description: If another chat later changed the same things, the first call changes NOTHING and lists those chats -> tell the operator 'this also undoes X from chat Y', ask. true ONLY after they agree; that call waits for the operator's click.

tools.name: start_isolated_branch
tools.description:
Move THIS chat from the shared draft (chats see each other's unstaged changes) onto its own isolated branch; later calls write there.
USE FOR (call FIRST, before any change): operator explicitly wants to try/experiment ('try a redesign', 'show me an alternative') | starting a site migration (site-migrate skill). Not for ordinary edits.
Only while this chat has no unstaged changes; else ask the operator to start a new experiment chat (Live edit -> New experiment).

reason.description: `experiment` = TRY something without touching the shared draft; `migration` = site migration/import.

tools.name: list_media_usages
tools.description: List modules whose HTML embeds one media asset (id from `find_media`). Use before replacing/deleting an image, or after `regenerate_media_variants` skipped a variant, to know which modules to edit.

tools.name: get_page_seo
tools.description:
Read pages' stored SEO fields (meta description, OG image, canonical, noindex, sitemap, autofill/optimize times) AND core text (plain text of own content blocks, no header/footer chrome, this chat's draft, ~1500 chars).
USE FOR: reading before writing/optimizing descriptions — ALL pages in one call, then ONE `autofill_page_seo_many` (first description) or `bulk_optimize_seo`/`set_page_seo_many`.
DO NOT USE `inspect_page_render`/`screenshot_page` for this (layout/visual only). No SEO row -> `autofill_page_seo_many` fills it.

tools.name: list_stale_seo_pages
tools.description: List pages whose SEO was never optimized or whose meta description is empty (newest first) — the dashboard's 'needs SEO' tile. Then: empty, never-autofilled -> `autofill_page_seo_many`; re-optimize with context -> `bulk_optimize_seo`; exact values -> `set_page_seo_many`.

tools.name: refresh_page_path
tools.description: Recompute ONE page's URL from its current data. DRAFT page -> moves now. PUBLISHED page with outdated URL -> not moved; result reports awaiting a URL migration -> call `propose_url_migration` (Owner-approved; previews the move + writes 301s). Linking/unlinking language variants already refreshes touched pages. Not for renaming (`update_pages_many` with a new slug).

redirectFromOld.description: 'auto' (default) 301s the old URL when it moved.

tools.name: list_import_runs
tools.description: List site-import (migration) runs, newest first: id, source URL, status, pages seen/extracted, errors. Use to find a run id not proposed in this chat, or check whether an approved crawl finished. Per-run detail: `get_import_run_report`.

tools.name: log_import_events
tools.description: Record findings in import-run event ledgers (the migration report the operator reads): skipped assets, fidelity gaps, inventory mismatches, compose problems. `phase` e.g. crawl|media|fidelity|inventory|compose; `detail` = optional structured data. Send ALL findings of a step in ONE call (may span runs); all insert or none. Notes on one imported page -> `add_import_page_notes`.

tools.name: list_skill_pin_defaults
tools.description: List skills pinned to engage in every new chat. Read before `set_skill_pin_defaults` (replaces the whole list).

tools.name: set_skill_pin_defaults
tools.description: Set which skills engage automatically in every NEW chat of the operator you act for (e.g. 'always pin scoped-edit'). Per-person; current chat unaffected (`load_skill` engages now).

slugs.description: Active skill slugs. FULL list (read `list_skill_pin_defaults` first); omitted ones are unpinned; [] clears.

tools.name: list_list_types
tools.description:
Read the site's list types — the shapes lists take: node kinds, fields (`*` = required), nesting, nodes that generate entries from a source (page query, breadcrumbs, plugin). Read before writing list entries or a module's `{{#field}}…{{/field}}` template (node fields = keys inside the section).
- Menus, navigation, footer links, categories, tags = SHARED LISTS of a fitting type; no menu-specific tools. A list ONE module shows stays LOCAL (entries in its `list` field); used in several places, site navigation or a page vocabulary -> SHARED; `promote_local_list` switches local -> shared.
- Shipped: `texts` (strings), `links` (label + link), `menu` (nested, 3 levels, marks current page), `categories`/`tags` (vocabularies pages are assigned to).
- 'ships with plugin' = read-only definition (fill its lists). 'Inert plugin settings' = extensions of an inactive plugin, kept, not applied.
- No type fits (mega menu with columns + latest news, team list with photo + role) -> `upsert_list_types_many`; don't bend `links`.

slug.description: One type in detail + every list and module using it.

query.description: Free text over slug, name, purpose.

tools.name: upsert_list_types_many
tools.description:
Create or replace list types (the SHAPE of a list) in one transaction.
DO NOT USE FOR: a near-duplicate of a shipped type (reuse `links`/`menu`); changing a plugin-shipped type (create your own slug).
CORE RULES:
- `nodes`: node kind -> {label, fields, children:{name, allow}, source, current_from}. `root.allow` = top-level node kinds. `purpose` = why the type exists (later reads decide by it). `max_depth` required when a node allows itself.
- Field semantics: `link` value = {href}; `module` = embedded module (`accepts`: module types, absent = any); `term` = entries of vocabulary list `list`. `current_from` names the node's link field that marks the current page.
- Vocabulary types: exactly one node kind, with text fields `name` + `slug`.
- `source` -> generated entries instead of stored children: `query` (`editable` = knobs an entry may change, `defaults` = query), `system`, `plugin`.
- Mega menu example: root.allow ["column","link"]; `column` {fields:[heading text*], children:{name:"links", allow:["link","news"]}}; `link` {fields:[label text*, link link*], current_from:"link"}; `news` {fields:[heading text], source:{kind:"query", editable:["limit"], defaults:{page_type:"news", order:"published_desc", limit:3}}} (`*` = required:true).
- Changes are checked against every list of the type (incl. local lists in modules): a new required field needs a `default`; removing a node kind/field that has values is refused naming the lists -> `dropValues:true` only when the operator agreed to lose them.
- `expectedVersion` from `list_list_types` prevents overwriting a concurrent change.

tools.name: delete_list_types_many
tools.description: Delete list types by slug. Refused for plugin-shipped types and while any list (shared, or local in a module field) uses the type — the error names them; delete or convert those first. Undoable. Not for emptying a list (`patch_list_items_many`/`upsert_lists_many`) or dropping one (`delete_lists_many`).

tools.name: list_lists
tools.description:
The site's SHARED lists (TOON rows): slug, type, role, entry count, purpose, binding module fields (module.field), placements, sample pages, vocabulary use, last edit. Entries -> `get_list`.
Call BEFORE creating a list: 'add Careers to the menu' -> the header's list is here (usedBy = header module) -> patch it, never mint a second menu.
Menus, nav, footer links, categories, tags = SHARED LISTS of a fitting type (menu, links, categories, tags, custom e.g. mega menu); no menu-specific tools. Shown by ONE module -> LOCAL (its `list` field); >1 place, site nav or a page vocabulary -> SHARED (`promote_local_list` converts). Local lists are not listed here -> `list_modules`.

query.description: Free text over slug, name, purpose, entry text.

tools.name: get_list
tools.description: One shared list (by `slug` or `id`): entry tree (ids, node kinds, values, links as paths), `version`, usage. Read before `patch_list_items_many`: patches address entries by id (Careers under Company -> `parentId` = Company's id); pass `version` as `expectedVersion`.

tools.name: upsert_lists_many
tools.description:
Create shared lists or replace a list's WHOLE entry tree (one tx).
Menus, nav, footer links, categories, tags = SHARED LISTS of a fitting type (menu, links, categories, tags, custom e.g. mega menu); no menu-specific tools. Shown by ONE module -> LOCAL (its `list` field); >1 place, site nav or a page vocabulary -> SHARED (`promote_local_list` converts).
DO NOT USE FOR changing a few entries -> `patch_list_items_many` (a replace drops every omitted entry).
Then bind it: module `list` field with `bind:'shared'`, `list:'caelo:list/<id>'` (`add_module` / `update_modules_many`), e.g. the layout header.

purpose.description: Why + where it shows, e.g. 'Main navigation in the site header'.

items.description: WHOLE entry tree. Keep `id` of existing entries, omit for new. `values` keyed by the node's fields; terms `caelo:term/<listId>/<itemId>`. `children` only under nodes allowing them. `query` only on source nodes, only the knobs its source lists in `editable` (e.g. {limit:5}); omit = type `defaults`. Links `{href}`: internal path (`/about`) of an EXISTING page (`list_pages`; else build an empty shell first: `build_page` with `modules: []`); `/` and `/#section` always valid; pages of an import run rebuilt in this chat are kept for `resolve_import_links`; external = full `https://` URL. E.g. (menu): [{"node":"entry","values":{"label":"Company","link":{"href":"/about"}},"children":[{"node":"entry","values":{"label":"Team","link":{"href":"/about/team"}}}]}]

tools.name: patch_list_items_many
tools.description:
Edit shared-list entries by id — the routine way to maintain a menu, footer links or a vocabulary (one tx). Every page showing the list updates; nothing to rewire. Result names added entry ids.
`add`: omit `parentId` = top level, omit `position` = append. `update`: `values` merged, `null` removes a value. `remove`: drops its children too.
'Add Careers under Company' = `get_list` -> one `add` with `parentId` = Company's id. Pass `expectedVersion` from `get_list`; conflict = list changed -> re-read, redo.

tools.name: delete_lists_many
tools.description: Delete shared lists by slug (undoable). Refused while a module field/placement binds one (error names them) -> rebind/remove first. Entries -> `patch_list_items_many`; list types -> `delete_list_types_many`.

tools.name: promote_local_list
tools.description: Turn a module's LOCAL list into a SHARED list and bind the field to it, in one call — when a second place needs the same entries ('footer links in the mobile menu too', 'editors maintain these links without opening the module'). `field` = the module's `list` field. Refused when placements show different entries (names them) -> pick the entries to keep, use `upsert_lists_many` + `update_modules_many`. Returns list id + ref `caelo:list/<id>` for binding other modules.

tools.name: preview_list_source
tools.description:
Show what a generated list (page query, system or plugin source) returns for a page BEFORE binding/saving it; same resolver as preview + build, this chat's draft view. Only published pages appear; empty = wrong filter (page type slug, terms) or nothing published yet.
Name the source ONE way:
- `source` (+ `value` overrides, `vocabulary` for page_terms), e.g. {source:{kind:'query', editable:['limit'], defaults:{page_type:'news', order:'published_desc', limit:3}}}
- `list` + `itemId`: saved source node of a shared list (e.g. mega menu's news column)
- `list` + `node` + `value`: a source node kind of the list's type with the knobs about to be saved
- `moduleId` + `field` (+ `contentInstanceId`): a module's source field.
`pageId` = page it renders on; needed for breadcrumbs/children/siblings/page_terms; a query excludes that page.

tools.name: list_page_types
tools.description: The site's page types, what each page IS (`page`, `news`, `product`): purpose, page count, allowed + default template ids, properties (`*` = required), vocabularies (categories/tags lists whose terms its pages carry). Read before `build_page` / `update_pages_many` (a new article gets `pageType:"news"` + its properties and terms) and before a page query (`page_type` filters on the slug). New KIND of content (blog, job board) -> `upsert_page_types_many`.

slug.description: One type in detail, with sample pages.

query.description: Free text over slug, name, purpose.

tools.name: upsert_page_types_many
tools.description:
Create or replace page types in one transaction, when the operator starts a new kind of content ('a news section with categories', 'a job board').
CORE RULES:
- `templates`: ids from `list_templates`; none fits -> `create_template` with `pageType` first. `defaultTemplate` is one of them.
- `properties`: fields every page of the type carries (e.g. `author` text, `event_date` date); no `module` fields. `vocabularies[].list`: list id from `list_lists`.
- Order for 'news with categories': `upsert_lists_many` (a `categories` list) -> `create_template` (pageType `news`) or reuse one -> this -> `build_page`/`update_pages_many` with pageType, properties, terms.
- Type in use: a new property's default is written into its pages; dropping a template they use is refused (move them first); dropping a property/vocabulary they hold values for needs `dropValues:true` (only with operator agreement). Pass `expectedVersion` from `list_page_types`.

tools.name: delete_page_types_many
tools.description: Delete page types by slug. Refused for the site's default type and while pages use it (move them first: `update_pages_many` `pageType`). Undoable.
